-- OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
-- SOFTWARE.

--!strict
-- Shared bounded execution results in the VM that calls run.
local LogService = game:GetService("LogService")
local LogBuffer = require(script.Parent.LogBuffer)
local Serialize = require(script.Parent.Serialize)
local Results = require(script.Parent.Results)
-- A chunk that prints in a loop would otherwise return a response no context
-- window can hold.
local MAX_OUTPUT_LINES = 200
local MAX_RETURN_VALUES = 10

-- Returned tables are walked rather than counted, but not without limit: a
-- chunk that returns a whole config tree, or one with a cycle in it, must not be
-- able to produce a response nothing can read.
local MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES = 50
local MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 4
type Budget = { nodes: number, chars: number, omitted: boolean? }

local function clipped(text: string, cap: number): string
	local last = cap
	while last > 0 do
		local byte = string.byte(text, last + 1)
		if byte < 128 or byte >= 192 then break end
		last -= 1
	end
	return string.sub(text, 1, last) .. "<truncated>"
end

local function describe(value: any, depth: number?, seen: { [any]: boolean }?, shared: Budget?): any
	local budget = shared or {nodes = 300, chars = 10000}
	budget.nodes -= 1
	budget.chars -= 30
	if budget.nodes < 0 or budget.chars < 100 then budget.omitted = true; return "<budget exceeded>" end
	local level = depth or 0
	local visited = seen or {}
	local kind = typeof(value)

	if kind == "function" or kind == "thread" then
		return string.format("<%s>", kind)
	end
	if kind ~= "table" then
		local result = Serialize.value(value)
		if typeof(result) == "string" then
			local cap = math.min(2000, math.floor(budget.chars / 6))
			budget.chars -= math.min(#result, cap) * 6
			if #result > cap then budget.omitted = true end
			return if #result > cap then clipped(result, cap) else result
		end
		return result
	end

	local source = value :: { [any]: any }
	-- Named separately from the depth cap, because they mean opposite things to
	-- a reader. The depth cap says "there is more below this"; a cycle says
	-- "this is the table you are already inside". Reporting the second as the
	-- first printed `t.self.self.self` as three distinct nested tables, which
	-- reads as real structure that does not exist.
	if visited[source] then
		return "<circular reference>"
	end
	if level >= MAX_TABLE_DEPTH then
		budget.omitted = true
		return "<nested table>"
	end
	visited[source] = true

	local count = 0
	local isArray = true
	for key in source do
		if typeof(key) ~= "number" or key < 1 or key > #source or key % 1 ~= 0 then isArray = false end
		count += 1
		if count > MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES then break end
	end

	-- Arrays keep their shape so they read as lists on the other side; anything
	-- with non-sequential keys becomes a map with stringified keys.
	if isArray and (count == #source or count > MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES) then
		local list: { any } = {}
		for index, item in ipairs(source) do
			if index > MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES or budget.nodes <= 0 or budget.chars < 100 then
				budget.omitted = true
				table.insert(list, "<more entries>")
				break
			end
			table.insert(list, describe(item, level + 1, visited, budget))
		end
		-- Cleared on the way out so the same table appearing twice side by side
		-- still renders twice; only a table containing itself is a cycle.
		visited[source] = nil
		return list
	end

	local map: { [string]: any } = {}
	local shown = 0
	for key, item in source do
		shown += 1
		if shown > MAX_TABLE_ENTRIES or budget.nodes <= 0 or budget.chars < 100 then
			budget.omitted = true
			map["..."] = "<more entries>"
			break
		end
		local name = string.sub(tostring(key), 1, 100)
		budget.chars -= #name * 6
		map[name] = describe(item, level + 1, visited, budget)
	end
	visited[source] = nil
	return map
end

local Runtime = {}
Runtime.describe = describe
-- `stopped` is polled while the chunk yields; true abandons it (the caller cancelled).
function Runtime.run(chunk: () -> ...any, timeout: number?, stopped: (() -> boolean)?): { [string]: any }
	-- Captured rather than inferred: a chunk's prints are usually the point, and
	-- reading them back from the log afterwards would also pick up whatever else
	-- the place logged in the meantime.
	local output: { { [string]: any } } = {}
	local fullOutput: { { [string]: any } } = {}
	local fullOutputBytes = 0
	local outputTruncated = false
	local outputChars, outputDropped = 0, 0
	local connection = LogService.MessageOut:Connect(function(message, messageType, context)
		if #fullOutput < MAX_OUTPUT_LINES and fullOutputBytes + #message <= 131072 then
			fullOutputBytes += #message
			table.insert(fullOutput, { message = message, level = tostring(messageType) })
		end
		if #output < MAX_OUTPUT_LINES and outputChars < 8000 then
			-- A structured log's context rides on the line, as it does in `console`.
			local encoded = LogBuffer.encodeContext(context)
			if encoded then
				message ..= "  " .. encoded
			end
			if #message > math.min(2000, 8000 - outputChars) then
				outputTruncated = true
				message = clipped(message, math.min(2000, 8000 - outputChars))
			end
			outputChars += #message
			table.insert(output, {
				message = message,
				level = if messageType == Enum.MessageType.MessageError
					then "error"
					elseif messageType == Enum.MessageType.MessageWarning then "warning"
					elseif messageType == Enum.MessageType.MessageInfo then "info"
					else "print",
			})
		else outputDropped += 1 end
	end)

	local started = os.clock()
	local results: any = nil
	if timeout or stopped then
		-- A chunk that never yields finishes inside task.spawn, so the common
		-- case pays nothing for being stoppable.
		local worker = task.spawn(function() results = table.pack(pcall(chunk :: any)) end)
		local deadline = if timeout then started + timeout else math.huge
		local abandoned = false
		while results == nil and os.clock() < deadline do
			if stopped and stopped() then
				abandoned = true
				break
			end
			task.wait()
		end
		if results == nil then
			task.cancel(worker)
			results = table.pack(
				false,
				if abandoned
					then "CANCELLED: the request was cancelled while the code was still running"
					else "CLIENT_TIMEOUT: execution exceeded " .. tostring(timeout) .. "s"
			)
		end
	else
		results = table.pack(pcall(chunk :: () -> ...any))
	end
	local elapsed = os.clock() - started

	--[[
		MessageOut is deferred: `print` returns before the event fires, so
		disconnecting straight after the chunk finished captured nothing at all.
		A short settle picks the lines up.

		It is bounded and stops as soon as the flow stops, rather than waiting a
		fixed period, so a chunk that logged nothing costs almost no time and one
		that logged plenty is not truncated.
	]]
	local settleDeadline = os.clock() + 0.5
	local seen = #output
	local quietFrames = 0
	while os.clock() < settleDeadline and quietFrames < 3 do
		task.wait()
		if #output == seen then
			quietFrames += 1
		else
			seen = #output
			quietFrames = 0
		end
	end

	connection:Disconnect()

	if not results[1] then
		return {
			ok = false,
			error = string.sub(tostring(results[2]), 1, 2000),
			output = output,
			milliseconds = math.floor(elapsed * 1000 + 0.5),
		}
	end

	local returned: { any } = {}
	local budget: Budget = {nodes = 300, chars = 6000}
	for index = 2, math.min(results.n, MAX_RETURN_VALUES + 1) do
		-- A nil return is written out rather than dropped. `table.insert` of nil
		-- does nothing, so `return a, nil, b` came back as two values and every
		-- one after the nil shifted into the wrong position.
		local value = results[index]
		table.insert(returned, if value == nil then "nil" else describe(value, nil, nil, budget))
	end

	local response: { [string]: any } = {
		ok = true,
		returned = returned,
		outputDropped = if outputDropped > 0 then outputDropped else nil,
		returnsDropped = if results.n > MAX_RETURN_VALUES + 1 then results.n - MAX_RETURN_VALUES - 1 else nil,
		output = output,
		milliseconds = math.floor(elapsed * 1000 + 0.5),
	}
	if budget.omitted or outputTruncated or outputDropped > 0 or response.returnsDropped then
		local fullReturned: { any } = {}
		for index = 2, results.n do
			table.insert(fullReturned, if results[index] == nil then "nil" else results[index])
		end
		local notRetained = #output + outputDropped - #fullOutput
		local retained = Results.capture({ returned = fullReturned, output = fullOutput,
			outputNotRetained = if notRetained > 0 then notRetained else nil })
		for key, value in retained do response[key] = value end
		response.truncated = true
		response.outputNotRetained = if notRetained > 0 then notRetained else nil
	end
	return response
end
return Runtime

Four pure functions, pulled out of `Console` so they can be tested. That is the whole reason this file exists, and it is a good one: every function here has already shipped a visible bug -- a paragraph that wrapped back to column 0 under the timestamps, a stray "m" on its own line, raw `**` in the middle of a sentence -- and each of those was found by looking at a screenshot rather than by a test, because `Console` requires half of Studio and cannot be bundled outside it. Nothing in here requires anything, touches an Instance, or reads a palette. Colour arrives as a hex string the caller has already resolved, so the module never needs Color3 and the same code runs under the standalone Luau interpreter that `npm test` drives. ]] local Format = {} --[[ Breaks a long string into lines at word boundaries. Roblox's own TextWrapped would do this, and would wrap to column 0 -- there is no hanging indent for a TextLabel -- which is the ragged shape this replaces. Wrapping here means every continuation line can carry the indent. A single word longer than the width is cut rather than allowed to overhang. That case is not prose: it is a path, a URL or a base64 blob, and letting one of those push the line out re-creates the exact wrap this exists to prevent. ]] function Format.wrap(text: string, width: number): { string } local lines: { string } = {} local current = "" local function flush() if current ~= "" then table.insert(lines, current) current = "" end end for word in string.gmatch(text, "%S+") do while (utf8.len(word) or #word) > width do flush() local cut = utf8.offset(word, width + 1) or (width + 1) table.insert(lines, string.sub(word, 1, cut - 1)) word = string.sub(word, cut) end local candidate = if current == "" then word else current .. " " .. word if (utf8.len(candidate) or #candidate) > width and current ~= "" then flush() current = word else current = candidate end end flush() return lines end -- RichText is markup, so anything user- or engine-supplied has to be escaped or -- a stray `<` in an error message silently eats the rest of the line. function Format.escape(value: string): string local escaped = string.gsub(value, "&", "&") escaped = string.gsub(escaped, "<", "<") escaped = string.gsub(escaped, ">", ">") return escaped end --[[ Turns an agent's markdown into the markup this label already speaks. Agents write for a terminal that renders markdown, so their replies arrive full of `**` and backticks. Printed raw they are worse than noise -- the asterisks land in the middle of a sentence and read as typos -- and stripping them would throw away the emphasis the agent chose. The label is RichText, so the third option is simply to honour it. Must be applied AFTER `escape`, which is what makes it safe: escaping has already turned every angle bracket in the agent's own text into an entity, so the only tags in the string afterwards are the ones put there here. Bold before italic, or the outer pair of a `**` run is eaten as two italics. Underscores are deliberately not italic markers: `execute_luau` and `mcp__rbx-studio__modify` are the vocabulary of this log, and they would spend most of their lives in italics for no reason. `code` is a "#RRGGBB" string rather than a Color3 so this module stays free of the engine; the caller has a palette and this does not. ]] function Format.emphasise(escaped: string, code: string): string local marked = string.gsub(escaped, "%*%*(.-)%*%*", "%1") marked = string.gsub(marked, "`([^`]+)`", function(inner: string): string return string.format('%s', code, inner) end) marked = string.gsub(marked, "%*([^%*]+)%*", "%1") return marked end --[[ Collapses anything that would break the one-line-per-row contract. A row is a line. Every width in the console is measured in characters and every continuation is indented by hand, so a newline arriving inside a message or a detail lands in the middle of that arithmetic and comes out at column 0 -- which is how a two-line Luau snippet in a tool argument left a bare "m" sitting under the log. Tabs go the same way, for the same reason. ]] function Format.flatten(text: string): string return (string.gsub(text, "%s+", " ")) end return Format

--!strict
-- Session-local instance references. Nothing is written to the place. Roblox
-- can collect a Lua Instance wrapper even while the engine instance is still
-- parented, so addressable handles need bounded strong references, not weak
-- values. Deleted/detached instances are refused and released on lookup.
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")
local Dispatch = require(script.Parent.Dispatch)

local Handles = {}
local prefix = "@mcp:" .. HttpService:GenerateGUID(false) .. ":"
local nextId = 0
local ids: { [Instance]: number } = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" }) :: any
local values: { [number]: Instance } = {}
local CAPACITY = 5000
local ring: { [number]: number } = {}
local slot = 0

-- A stable number for ordering same-named siblings. Allocating one takes no
-- handle slot: sorting a large folder must not evict handles already issued.
function Handles.id(instance: Instance): number
	local id = ids[instance]
	if not id then
		nextId += 1
		id = nextId
		ids[instance] = id
	end
	return id
end

-- Only handed-out handles occupy the bounded cache. Old handles fail rather
-- than point at a replacement with the same name.
function Handles.of(instance: Instance): string
	local id = Handles.id(instance)
	if values[id] == nil then
		slot = slot % CAPACITY + 1
		local previous = ring[slot]
		if previous then values[previous] = nil end
		ring[slot] = id
		values[id] = instance
	end
	return prefix .. tostring(id)
end

function Handles.resolve(handle: string): Instance
	local suffix = if string.sub(handle, 1, #prefix) == prefix then string.sub(handle, #prefix + 1) else ""
	local id = tonumber(suffix)
	local instance = if id then values[id] else nil
	if instance == nil or (instance ~= game and not instance:IsDescendantOf(game)) then
		if id then values[id] = nil end
		Dispatch.fail("STALE_HANDLE", "This handle is expired, destroyed, or belongs to another session/client.",
			"Query the instance again in the same context. A handle never falls back to a name lookup.")
	end
	return instance :: Instance
end

return Handles

-- SOFTWARE.

--!strict
--[[
	The console log, carried across the boundaries that used to erase it.

	Pressing Play does not pause this plugin, it loads a second and a third copy
	of it into the playtest's DataModels, each with its own empty console. Studio
	then shows you the play view's panel, so the session you were watching
	appears to have been wiped; stopping the test shows the editor's again, and
	everything that happened during the test is missing from it instead. Nothing
	crashed and nothing was lost -- the log was simply written in a window that is
	no longer the one on screen.

	Two halves fix that, and they are deliberately different mechanisms because
	the two directions have different problems.

	Forwards (editor -> playtest) is a cold start: the playtest's copies begin
	with nothing and need what was already on screen. That is persistence, and it
	is what this file does -- the edit session writes its rows to plugin
	settings, and every copy reads them once at load.

	Backwards (playtest -> editor) is not persistence at all. The editor session
	is still running the whole time; it just is not the one being asked to do the
	work. So there is nothing to restore, only something to be told, and it is
	told over the bridge -- see `settle` in the server's bridge/rpc.rs.

	Only the EDIT session writes. It is the one that outlives every playtest and
	receives the peer announcements, so its log is the superset; letting the
	playtest copies write as well would store the same rows twice and replay both
	on the next load.
]]

local History = {}

local SETTING = "consoleHistory"

--[[
	Rows kept, well under the console's own 300.

	This is a settings file, rewritten in full on every save, and the value of an
	old row falls off quickly -- what you want back is the screenful you were
	looking at when the playtest started, not yesterday afternoon.
]]
local MAX_ROWS = 150

--[[
	Seconds between saves.

	A burst of commands writes several rows a second and every one of them would
	otherwise be a rewrite of the whole file. The loss window is the same two
	seconds, and the only way to lose that window is to close Studio inside it --
	which `flush` covers anyway.
]]
local SAVE_EVERY = 2

export type Row = {
	level: string,
	message: string,
	detail: string?,
	stamp: string,
	-- Threadline shape, so a carried log keeps its threads and latency bars.
	turn: boolean?,
	threaded: boolean?,
	ms: number?,
	-- A grouped row's sub-items.
	children: { { message: string, detail: string? } }?,
}

local store: Plugin? = nil
local read: (() -> { Row })? = nil
local dirty = false
local running = false

--[[
	Which place this log belongs to.

	One settings file is shared by every Studio window on the machine, so without
	a key a second place's session would read back the first's history and show
	it as its own. An unsaved place has no id, so its name stands in -- imperfect
	between two unsaved places, and better than merging them.
]]
local function placeKey(): string
	if game.PlaceId ~= 0 then
		return tostring(game.PlaceId)
	end
	return "local:" .. game.Name
end

--[[
	Rows survive a round trip through JSON, so nothing that comes back is
	trusted: a settings file is a file on disk, and a field that is missing or
	the wrong type must skip the row rather than reach the renderer.
]]
local function sane(value: any): Row?
	if typeof(value) ~= "table" then
		return nil
	end
	local row = value :: { [string]: any }
	if typeof(row.level) ~= "string" or typeof(row.message) ~= "string" then
		return nil
	end
	if typeof(row.stamp) ~= "string" then
		return nil
	end
	-- A group's sub-items, each checked like a row: anything malformed is dropped.
	local children: { { message: string, detail: string? } }? = nil
	if typeof(row.children) == "table" then
		local kept = {}
		for _, child in row.children do
			if typeof(child) == "table" and typeof(child.message) == "string" then
				table.insert(kept, {
					message = child.message,
					detail = if typeof(child.detail) == "string" then child.detail else nil,
				})
			end
		end
		if #kept > 0 then
			children = kept
		end
	end
	return {
		children = children,
		level = row.level,
		message = row.message,
		detail = if typeof(row.detail) == "string" then row.detail else nil,
		stamp = row.stamp,
		turn = if row.turn == true then true else nil,
		threaded = if row.threaded == true then true else nil,
		ms = if typeof(row.ms) == "number" then row.ms else nil,
	}
end

--[[
	`snapshot` is a function rather than rows, because saving is throttled: what
	must be written is whatever the console holds when the timer fires, not what
	it held when the row that triggered it was logged.
]]
function History.attach(pluginObject: Plugin, snapshot: () -> { Row })
	store = pluginObject
	read = snapshot
end

function History.restore(): { Row }
	local pluginObject = store
	if pluginObject == nil then
		return {}
	end
	local saved = pluginObject:GetSetting(SETTING)
	if typeof(saved) ~= "table" then
		return {}
	end
	local record = saved :: { [string]: any }
	if record.place ~= placeKey() or typeof(record.rows) ~= "table" then
		return {}
	end
	local rows: { Row } = {}
	for _, entry in record.rows :: { any } do
		local row = sane(entry)
		if row ~= nil then
			table.insert(rows, row)
		end
	end
	return rows
end

--[[
	Writes now. Called from the save loop and from `plugin.Unloading`, where
	there is no next tick to wait for.
]]
function History.flush()
	local pluginObject, snapshot = store, read
	if pluginObject == nil or snapshot == nil then
		return
	end
	dirty = false
	local rows = snapshot()
	while #rows > MAX_ROWS do
		table.remove(rows, 1)
	end
	-- Guarded because a settings write is disk I/O: a full disk or a locked file
	-- must cost the console its history, not its session.
	pcall(function()
		pluginObject:SetSetting(SETTING, { place = placeKey(), rows = rows })
	end)
end

-- Marks the log as changed. Cheap on purpose: it runs on every logged row.
function History.touch()
	dirty = true
end

--[[
	Starts the save loop. Owned here rather than by the caller so the throttle
	and the thing it throttles cannot drift apart.
]]
function History.start()
	running = true
	task.spawn(function()
		while running do
			task.wait(SAVE_EVERY)
			if running and dirty then
				History.flush()
			end
		end
	end)
end

-- Stops the loop on unload. A reloaded plugin is a fresh module, so without
-- this every reload would leave another timer running against a dead session.
function History.stop()
	running = false
end

return History

--!strict
--[[
	The header's icons, drawn as vector paths and animated by re-posing them.

	Path2D draws real curves at any size. Each icon is a set of strokes in a
	16x16 box; a stroke is a list of points with optional Bezier handles. To
	animate, a stroke is re-posed -- rotated, lifted -- and its control points
	written again, which keeps the lines crisp where rotating a frame would not
	(a GuiObject's Rotation does not carry its descendants).
]]

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Icons = {}

type Pt = { x: number, y: number, ix: number?, iy: number?, ox: number?, oy: number? }
type Stroke = { points: { Pt }, closed: boolean?, group: string? }
type Pose = { angle: number, cx: number, cy: number, dx: number, dy: number }

export type Drawn = {
	kind: string,
	scale: number,
	strokes: { Stroke },
	paths: { Path2D },
	poses: { [string]: Pose },
}

local function rotate(x: number, y: number, pose: Pose): (number, number)
	local a = math.rad(pose.angle)
	local c, s = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
	local rx, ry = x - pose.cx, y - pose.cy
	return pose.cx + rx * c - ry * s + pose.dx, pose.cy + rx * s + ry * c + pose.dy
end

local function turn(x: number, y: number, pose: Pose): (number, number)
	local a = math.rad(pose.angle)
	local c, s = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
	return x * c - y * s, x * s + y * c
end

-- A clockwise arc of `sweep` degrees from `from` (screen angles, y down).
local function arc(cx: number, cy: number, r: number, from: number, sweep: number, pieces: number): { Pt }
	local step = math.rad(sweep / pieces)
	local handle = 4 / 3 * math.tan(step / 4) * r
	local points: { Pt } = {}
	for i = 0, pieces do
		local a = math.rad(from) + step * i
		local tx, ty = -math.sin(a), math.cos(a)
		table.insert(points, {
			x = cx + r * math.cos(a),
			y = cy + r * math.sin(a),
			ix = -tx * handle,
			iy = -ty * handle,
			ox = tx * handle,
			oy = ty * handle,
		})
	end
	return points
end

local function line(...: number): { Pt }
	local values = { ... }
	local points: { Pt } = {}
	for i = 1, #values, 2 do
		table.insert(points, { x = values[i], y = values[i + 1] })
	end
	return points
end

-- Reload geometry: an arc open at the upper right, a solid arrowhead on its end.
Icons.RELOAD = { from = -5, sweep = 275, r = 5.6, cx = 8, cy = 8.6 }

local function strokesFor(kind: string): { Stroke }
	if kind == "reconnect" then
		local g = Icons.RELOAD
		local strokes: { Stroke } = { { points = arc(g.cx, g.cy, g.r, g.from, g.sweep, 4), group = "all" } }
		local a = math.rad(g.from + g.sweep)
		local ex, ey = g.cx + g.r * math.cos(a), g.cy + g.r * math.sin(a)
		local tx, ty = -math.sin(a), math.cos(a)
		local nx, ny = -ty, tx
		-- Base centred on the arc's end, tip ahead along its direction.
		local wide, tip = 2.1, 2.4
		table.insert(strokes, {
			points = line(
				ex + nx * wide, ey + ny * wide,
				ex + tx * tip, ey + ty * tip,
				ex - nx * wide, ey - ny * wide
			),
			closed = true,
			group = "all",
		})
		return strokes
	end
	return {
		{ points = line(2.5, 4.5, 13.5, 4.5), group = "lid" },
		{ points = line(6, 4.5, 6, 2.5, 10, 2.5, 10, 4.5), group = "lid" },
		{ points = line(4, 4.5, 4.8, 13.5, 11.2, 13.5, 12, 4.5), group = "body" },
		{ points = line(6.8, 7, 6.8, 11), group = "body" },
		{ points = line(9.2, 7, 9.2, 11), group = "body" },
	}
end

local REST: Pose = { angle = 0, cx = 8, cy = 8, dx = 0, dy = 0 }

local function apply(drawn: Drawn)
	local s = drawn.scale
	for index, stroke in drawn.strokes do
		local pose = drawn.poses[stroke.group or "all"] or REST
		local points = {}
		for _, p in stroke.points do
			local x, y = rotate(p.x, p.y, pose)
			local ix, iy = turn(p.ix or 0, p.iy or 0, pose)
			local ox, oy = turn(p.ox or 0, p.oy or 0, pose)
			table.insert(
				points,
				Path2DControlPoint.new(
					UDim2.fromOffset(x * s, y * s),
					UDim2.fromOffset(ix * s, iy * s),
					UDim2.fromOffset(ox * s, oy * s)
				)
			)
		end
		drawn.paths[index]:SetControlPoints(points)
	end
end

function Icons.draw(parent: GuiObject, kind: string, color: Color3, scale: number?): Drawn
	local s = scale or 1
	local box = Instance.new("Frame")
	box.Name = "Icon"
	box.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	box.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	box.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	box.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(16 * s, 16 * s)
	box.Parent = parent

	local drawn: Drawn = { kind = kind, scale = s, strokes = strokesFor(kind), paths = {}, poses = {} }
	for _, stroke in drawn.strokes do
		local path = Instance.new("Path2D")
		path.Color3 = color
		path.Thickness = 1.5 * s
		path.Closed = stroke.closed == true
		path.Parent = box
		table.insert(drawn.paths, path)
	end
	apply(drawn)
	return drawn
end

function Icons.setColor(drawn: Drawn, color: Color3)
	for _, path in drawn.paths do
		path.Color3 = color
	end
end

--[[
	Runs `frame(t)` for `seconds`, t going 0 to 1, posing the icon each frame.
	A newer animation on the same icon cancels the one in flight.
]]
local function animate(drawn: Drawn, seconds: number, frame: (number) -> ())
	local token = {}
	;(drawn :: any).running = token
	local started = os.clock()
	local connection: RBXScriptConnection
	connection = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
		if (drawn :: any).running ~= token then
			connection:Disconnect()
			return
		end
		local t = math.min(1, (os.clock() - started) / seconds)
		frame(t)
		apply(drawn)
		if t >= 1 then
			connection:Disconnect()
		end
	end)
end

local function easeOut(t: number): number
	return 1 - (1 - t) ^ 3
end

local function centre(): Pose
	local g = Icons.RELOAD
	return { angle = 0, cx = g.cx, cy = g.cy, dx = 0, dy = 0 }
end

-- Hover: the reload arrow leans a quarter turn ahead, the bin's lid lifts.
function Icons.hover(drawn: Drawn, on: boolean)
	if drawn.kind == "reconnect" then
		local pose = drawn.poses.all or centre()
		drawn.poses.all = pose
		local from = pose.angle
		local to = if on then 40 else 0
		animate(drawn, 0.25, function(t)
			pose.angle = from + (to - from) * easeOut(t)
		end)
	else
		local lid = drawn.poses.lid or { angle = 0, cx = 2.5, cy = 4.5, dx = 0, dy = 0 }
		drawn.poses.lid = lid
		local fromA, fromY = lid.angle, lid.dy
		local toA, toY = if on then -12 else 0, if on then -1.2 else 0
		animate(drawn, 0.2, function(t)
			local e = easeOut(t)
			lid.angle = fromA + (toA - fromA) * e
			lid.dy = fromY + (toY - fromY) * e
		end)
	end
end

-- Click: the reload arrow spins a full turn; the bin flips its lid and shudders.
function Icons.press(drawn: Drawn)
	if drawn.kind == "reconnect" then
		local pose = drawn.poses.all or centre()
		drawn.poses.all = pose
		local from = pose.angle
		animate(drawn, 0.6, function(t)
			pose.angle = from + 360 * easeOut(t)
			if t >= 1 then
				pose.angle = from
			end
		end)
	else
		local lid = drawn.poses.lid or { angle = 0, cx = 2.5, cy = 4.5, dx = 0, dy = 0 }
		local body = drawn.poses.body or { angle = 0, cx = 8, cy = 13.5, dx = 0, dy = 0 }
		drawn.poses.lid, drawn.poses.body = lid, body
		animate(drawn, 0.45, function(t)
			-- Lid snaps open then drops shut; the body rocks twice.
			local open = math.sin(math.min(t * 2, 1) * math.pi)
			lid.angle = -28 * open
			lid.dy = -2 * open
			body.angle = 7 * math.sin(t * math.pi * 4) * (1 - t)
		end)
	end
end

return Icons

--!strict
--[[
	The output log, kept ourselves.

	`LogService:GetLogHistory()` looks like the right API and cannot be relied on.
	Measured: in an editor session it returns a handful of lines from around
	startup and then stops growing -- prints made later never appear -- and in a
	playtest server's DataModel it succeeds and returns nothing at all, even
	immediately after something printed there. The call reports no error either
	way, so the tool built on it answered "the log is empty" for a place that was
	logging steadily, which is worse than answering nothing.

	`LogService.MessageOut` does fire reliably in both. So the buffer is filled
	from the event, seeded once from whatever history the API does offer, and kept
	from growing without bound.

	This has to be connected at plugin load rather than when a read arrives:
	anything logged before the first subscription is gone for good.
]]

local LogService = game:GetService("LogService")
local ScriptContext = game:GetService("ScriptContext")
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")

-- Roughly what the Output window keeps. Big enough that a playtest's worth of
-- logging survives, small enough to stay cheap to hold and to scan.
local CAPACITY = 2000

-- Trimming in batches rather than one entry per insert: a chunk that logs in a
-- loop would otherwise shift the whole array on every single line.
local SLACK = 500

-- How far back an arriving stack trace will look for the error line it belongs
-- to. The two events fire within moments of each other, so anything beyond a
-- handful of entries is a mismatch rather than a late delivery.
local CORRELATION_WINDOW = 20

-- A structured log's context, as JSON, is cut here: Roblox's own server logs
-- drop context past 1KiB, so nothing longer is worth carrying.
local MAX_CONTEXT = 1000

export type Entry = {
	sequence: number?,
	id: number?,
	updated: boolean?,
	level: string,
	message: string,
	timestamp: number,
	-- Present on errors once the matching stack trace has been correlated.
	stack: string?,
	source: string?,
	-- The table a structured log (`LogService:Info(msg, context)`) carried, as JSON.
	context: string?,
}

local LEVELS: { [number]: string } = {
	[Enum.MessageType.MessageOutput.Value] = "print",
	[Enum.MessageType.MessageInfo.Value] = "info",
	[Enum.MessageType.MessageWarning.Value] = "warning",
	[Enum.MessageType.MessageError.Value] = "error",
}

local LogBuffer = {}

local entries: { Entry } = {}
local dropped = 0
local started = false
local startedAt = 0
local studioToken = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false)
local nextSequence = 0
local clientBuffers: { [Player]: { token: string, entries: { Entry }, dropped: number, sequence: number, startedAt: number, ready: boolean, orphan: { [string]: { stack: string, source: string? } } } } = {}

--[[
	Stack traces that arrived before the error line they describe.

	`ScriptContext.Error` and `LogService.MessageOut` are independent events for
	the same failure and there is no guaranteed order between them, so the trace
	is held here until its line shows up rather than being dropped for arriving
	first.
]]
local orphanedStacks: { [string]: { stack: string, source: string? } } = {}
local orphanCount = 0

--[[
	The engine also writes each trace to the log as plain lines -- "Stack Begin",
	one "Script 'X', Line N" per frame, then "Stack End" -- which is how the
	Output window renders it. Having attached the trace to its error already,
	echoing those lines as ordinary entries is duplication that reads like
	unrelated output sitting under the failure.

	They are collected instead of stored, and serve as the fallback source of a
	trace when ScriptContext.Error is unavailable.
]]
local STACK_OPEN = "Stack Begin"
local STACK_CLOSE = "Stack End"

-- If a close never arrives -- a place that prints "Stack Begin" itself -- the
-- collected lines are released rather than swallowed indefinitely.
local MAX_STACK_LINES = 60

local collecting: { string }? = nil

local function pushEntry(entry: Entry)
	nextSequence += 1
	entry.sequence = nextSequence
	entry.id = nextSequence
	entry.message = string.sub(entry.message, 1, 2000)
	if entry.stack then entry.stack = string.sub(entry.stack, 1, 4000) end
	if entry.source then entry.source = string.sub(entry.source, 1, 500) end
	table.insert(entries, entry)

	if #entries > CAPACITY + SLACK then
		local excess = #entries - CAPACITY
		entries = table.move(entries, excess + 1, #entries, 1, {})
		dropped += excess
	end
end

-- Each player gets a separate stream and token. Rejoining, reconnecting to a
-- different server DataModel, or a plugin reload invalidates old cursors.
function LogBuffer.startClient(player: Player)
	-- A relay reinstalled after a respawn is the same player in the same session:
	-- keep its log and cursor. Only a player that left (stopClient) starts fresh.
	local existing = clientBuffers[player]
	if existing then
		existing.ready = false
		return
	end
	clientBuffers[player] = { token = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false), entries = {}, dropped = 0, sequence = 0, startedAt = os.time(), ready = false, orphan = {} }
end

function LogBuffer.stopClient(player: Player)
	clientBuffers[player] = nil
end

function LogBuffer.pushClient(player: Player, payload: any)
	local buffer = clientBuffers[player]
	if not buffer or typeof(payload) ~= "table" then return end
	if payload.kind == "ready" then buffer.ready = true; return end
	if payload.kind == "trace" then
		if typeof(payload.message) ~= "string" or typeof(payload.stack) ~= "string" then return end
		local traceMessage = string.sub(payload.message, 1, 2000)
		for index = #buffer.entries, math.max(1, #buffer.entries - CORRELATION_WINDOW + 1), -1 do
			local item = buffer.entries[index]
			if item.level == "error" and item.message == string.sub(payload.message, 1, 2000) and item.stack == nil then
				item.stack = string.sub(payload.stack, 1, 4000)
				item.source = if typeof(payload.source) == "string" then string.sub(payload.source, 1, 500) else nil
				buffer.sequence += 1
				item.sequence = buffer.sequence
				item.updated = true
				table.remove(buffer.entries, index)
				table.insert(buffer.entries, item)
				return
			end
		end
		local orphanCount = 0
		for _ in buffer.orphan do orphanCount += 1 end
		if orphanCount < 20 or buffer.orphan[traceMessage] ~= nil then
			buffer.orphan[traceMessage] = { stack = string.sub(payload.stack, 1, 4000), source = if typeof(payload.source) == "string" then string.sub(payload.source, 1, 500) else nil }
		end
		return
	end
	local level = payload.level
	if level ~= "print" and level ~= "info" and level ~= "warning" and level ~= "error" then return end
	if typeof(payload.message) ~= "string" then return end
	buffer.sequence += 1
	local entry: Entry = {
		sequence = buffer.sequence,
		id = buffer.sequence,
		level = level,
		message = string.sub(payload.message, 1, 2000),
		timestamp = if typeof(payload.timestamp) == "number" and payload.timestamp >= 0 and payload.timestamp < 100000000000 then payload.timestamp else os.time(),
		stack = if typeof(payload.stack) == "string" then string.sub(payload.stack, 1, 4000) else nil,
		source = if typeof(payload.source) == "string" then string.sub(payload.source, 1, 500) else nil,
		context = if typeof(payload.context) == "string" then string.sub(payload.context, 1, MAX_CONTEXT) else nil,
	}
	local waiting = buffer.orphan[entry.message]
	if level == "error" and waiting then
		entry.stack, entry.source = waiting.stack, waiting.source
		buffer.orphan[entry.message] = nil
	end
	table.insert(buffer.entries, entry)
	if #buffer.entries > CAPACITY + SLACK then
		local excess = #buffer.entries - CAPACITY
		buffer.entries = table.move(buffer.entries, excess + 1, #buffer.entries, 1, {})
		buffer.dropped += excess
	end
end

function LogBuffer.clientReady(player: Player): boolean
	local buffer = clientBuffers[player]
	return buffer ~= nil and buffer.ready == true
end

function LogBuffer.stream(player: Player?): ({ Entry }, number, string, number, number)
	if player then
		local buffer = clientBuffers[player]
		if buffer then
			return table.move(buffer.entries, 1, #buffer.entries, 1, {}), buffer.dropped, buffer.token, buffer.sequence, math.max(0, os.time() - buffer.startedAt)
		end
		return {}, 0, "", 0, 0
	end
	return table.move(entries, 1, #entries, 1, {}), dropped, studioToken, nextSequence, LogBuffer.recordingSeconds()
end

--[[
	The context table of a structured log, as compact JSON.

	`LogService:Info("{player} leveled up", { player = "Bob" })` prints only the
	filled-in message; the table is the part that says which player and what
	state, and MessageOut hands it over as a third argument. Plain prints pass an
	empty table, which is dropped. Capped at 1000 characters -- the ceiling
	Roblox's own server logs apply -- and a table JSON cannot hold (a Vector3, an
	Instance) falls back to text rather than being lost.
]]
-- JSONEncode writes a Vector3 or an Instance as `null` without complaint, so
-- anything JSON has no shape for is turned into its text first.
local function plain(value: any, depth: number, budget: { nodes: number }): any
	budget.nodes -= 1
	if budget.nodes <= 0 then return "<truncated>" end
	local kind = typeof(value)
	if kind == "string" or kind == "number" or kind == "boolean" then
		return if kind == "string" then string.sub(value, 1, MAX_CONTEXT) else value
	elseif kind == "table" then
		if depth >= 4 then
			return "<table>"
		end
		local copy = {}
		for key, item in value do
			if budget.nodes <= 0 then copy["..."] = "<truncated>"; break end
			copy[if typeof(key) == "number" then key else string.sub(tostring(key), 1, 100)] = plain(item, depth + 1, budget)
		end
		return copy
	elseif kind == "Instance" then
		local ok, full = pcall(function()
			return value:GetFullName()
		end)
		return if ok then full else value.Name
	end
	return tostring(value)
end

function LogBuffer.encodeContext(context: any): string?
	if typeof(context) ~= "table" or next(context) == nil then
		return nil
	end
	local ok, encoded = pcall(function()
		return HttpService:JSONEncode(plain(context, 0, {nodes = 50}))
	end)
	if not ok then
		return nil
	end
	if #encoded > MAX_CONTEXT then return HttpService:JSONEncode({truncated = string.sub(encoded, 1, 100)}) end
	return encoded
end

local function push(message: string, messageType: Enum.MessageType, timestamp: number?, context: any?)
	message = string.sub(message, 1, 2000)
	local level = LEVELS[messageType.Value] or "print"
	local entry: Entry = {
		level = level,
		message = message,
		timestamp = timestamp or os.time(),
		context = LogBuffer.encodeContext(context),
	}

	-- Claim a trace that beat its own error line here.
	if level == "error" then
		local waiting = orphanedStacks[message]
		if waiting then
			entry.stack = waiting.stack
			entry.source = waiting.source
			orphanedStacks[message] = nil
			orphanCount -= 1
		end
	end

	pushEntry(entry)
end

--[[
	Attaches a stack trace to the error it belongs to.

	Correlated by message text because the engine offers nothing better: the two
	events carry no shared identifier. Matching the most recent unattached error
	with the same text is right in every case that matters, and the worst outcome
	if two identical errors interleave is that a trace lands on the wrong one of
	two identical lines.
]]
local function attachStack(message: string, stack: string, source: string?)
	message = string.sub(message, 1, 2000)
	stack = string.sub(stack, 1, 4000)
	if source then source = string.sub(source, 1, 500) end
	local first = math.max(1, #entries - CORRELATION_WINDOW + 1)
	for index = #entries, first, -1 do
		local entry = entries[index]
		if entry.level == "error" and entry.message == message and entry.stack == nil then
			entry.stack = stack
			entry.source = source
			nextSequence += 1
			entry.sequence = nextSequence
			entry.updated = true
			table.remove(entries, index)
			table.insert(entries, entry)
			return
		end
	end

	-- Not logged yet. Held for the line to claim, with a cap so a flood of
	-- errors that never surface cannot grow this without bound.
	if orphanCount < CAPACITY then
		if orphanedStacks[message] == nil then
			orphanCount += 1
		end
		orphanedStacks[message] = { stack = stack, source = source }
	end
end

--[[
	Begins recording. Safe to call more than once; only the first call connects,
	so a reload cannot end up with two subscriptions writing every line twice.
]]
function LogBuffer.start()
	if started then
		return
	end
	started = true
	startedAt = os.time()

	-- Seeded before subscribing so the backlog stays in order ahead of live
	-- lines. MessageOut only fires for messages after the connection, so nothing
	-- is counted twice.
	local ok, history = pcall(function()
		return LogService:GetLogHistory()
	end)
	if ok and typeof(history) == "table" then
		for _, item in history :: { { [string]: any } } do
			local kind = item.messageType
			if item.message ~= nil and typeof(kind) == "EnumItem" then
				push(tostring(item.message), kind :: Enum.MessageType, item.timestamp)
			end
		end
	end

	LogService.MessageOut:Connect(function(message: string, messageType: Enum.MessageType, context: any?)
		local buffered = collecting

		if buffered then
			if message == STACK_CLOSE then
				collecting = nil
				--[[
					ScriptContext.Error is preferred -- it names the originating
					instance too -- but not blindly. Measured on a nested failure
					the two agree exactly, one frame each, so folding loses
					nothing today. They are still compared by frame count rather
					than trusted to stay equal, because the cost of being wrong
					is a silently shallower trace and the check is one compare.
				]]
				if #buffered > 0 then
					local recent = entries[#entries]
					if recent and recent.level == "error" then
						local existing = recent.stack
						local existingFrames = if existing then #string.split(existing, "\n") else 0
						if existing == nil or #buffered > existingFrames then
							recent.stack = string.sub(table.concat(buffered, "\n"), 1, 4000)
							nextSequence += 1
							recent.sequence = nextSequence
							recent.updated = true
						end
					end
				end
				return
			end

			if #buffered < MAX_STACK_LINES then
				table.insert(buffered, message)
				return
			end

			-- Not a stack after all. Release what was held, in order, and carry
			-- on treating this as ordinary output.
			collecting = nil
			pushEntry({ level = "print", message = STACK_OPEN, timestamp = os.time() })
			for _, held in buffered do
				pushEntry({ level = "print", message = held, timestamp = os.time() })
			end
		elseif message == STACK_OPEN then
			collecting = {}
			return
		end

		push(message, messageType, nil, context)
	end)

	--[[
		Stack traces, which MessageOut does not carry.

		Without this an error in the log is a message and nothing else, while the
		trace arrives separately as loose "Stack Begin / Script X, Line N / Stack
		End" prints that read as unrelated output. Attaching it to the error turns
		three ambiguous lines into one answer with a script and a line number.

		`ErrorDetailed` would be the richer source and is closed to plugins --
		it needs the RobloxScript capability. `Error` is reachable and carries
		message, trace and originating script, which is the part that matters.
	]]
	pcall(function()
		ScriptContext.Error:Connect(function(message: string, stack: string, source: Instance?)
			local origin: string? = nil
			if typeof(source) == "Instance" then
				local named = pcall(function()
					origin = source:GetFullName()
				end)
				if not named then
					origin = source.Name
				end
			end
			attachStack(message, stack, origin)
		end)
	end)
end

--[[
	Everything held, oldest first, plus how much fell off the front. Returned as a
	copy so a caller filtering it cannot disturb the buffer.
]]
function LogBuffer.all(): ({ Entry }, number)
	return table.move(entries, 1, #entries, 1, {}), dropped
end

--[[
	How long this buffer has been recording, in seconds.

	An empty log is ambiguous without it. In a playtest the plugin loads at the
	same moment as the place's own scripts, so a script that logs on startup can
	beat the subscription -- and "nothing was logged" then looks identical to
	"recording began after the thing you are asking about". Reporting the window
	lets the two be told apart instead of guessed at.
]]
function LogBuffer.recordingSeconds(): number
	if not started then
		return 0
	end
	return math.max(0, os.time() - startedAt)
end

return LogBuffer

local Polaris = script:FindFirstAncestor("Polaris")
local App = Polaris.App
local Components = App.Components
local Util = Components.Util

local Fusion = require(Polaris.Packages.Fusion)

local Theme = require(App.Theme)
local stripProps = require(Util.stripProps)
local isState = require(Util.isState)

local IconButton = require(Components.IconButton)

local Value = Fusion.Value
local peek = Fusion.peek
local Hydrate = Fusion.Hydrate
local Computed = Fusion.Computed

local COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS = {
	"Changed",
	"Value",
	"Placeholder",
}

type Props = {
	Changed: ((value: boolean) -> ())?,
	Value: Fusion.CanBeState<boolean>?,
	Placeholder: Fusion.CanBeState<boolean>?,
	[any]: any,
}

return function(props: Props): TextButton
	local value = isState(props.Value) and props.Value or Value(props.Value or false)
	local placeholder = isState(props.Placeholder) and props.Placeholder or Value(props.Placeholder or false)

	return Hydrate(IconButton {
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(Theme.CompSizeY.Medium, Theme.CompSizeY.Medium),
		Solid = value,
		Blending = false,
		Glyph = "Check",
		GlyphColor = Computed(function(use)
			if use(value) then
				return use(Theme.Colors.TextBranded)
			elseif use(placeholder) then
				return use(Theme.Colors.TextDimmed)
			end

			return use(Theme.Colors.Background)
		end),
		Activated = function()
			value:set(not peek(value))

			if props.Changed then
				props.Changed(peek(value))
			end
		end,
	})(stripProps(props, COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS))
end

--!strict
--[[
	MicroProfiler captures, read through Roblox's own LibMP.

	The Script Performance window (`perf.profile`) only sees Luau. Most frame
	spikes are not Luau: physics, rendering, replication, a GC step, an engine
	job. The MicroProfiler sees all of it, scope by scope and thread by thread,
	and until now the only way to get it in front of an agent was a manual dump
	and a screenshot.

	LibMP (github.com/Roblox/libmp, MIT) is the official reader for
	`MicroProfilerService`'s binary channel. It is 3.3 MB of generated Luau, so it
	is NOT packed into the plugin: the server ships it and this module fetches it
	the first time a capture is asked for, then keeps it for the session. A
	plugin that never profiles never pays for it.

	Durations are attributed frame-locally (a scope that began in an earlier
	frame only counts from this frame's start), and self time is inclusive time
	minus the inclusive time of direct children -- the number that says where the
	work actually happened rather than which scope happened to contain it.
]]

local Dispatch = require(script.Parent.Dispatch)
local Net = require(script.Parent.Net)

local MicroProfiler = {}

local DEFAULT_FRAMES = 64
local MAX_FRAMES = 256
local DEFAULT_TOP = 20
local MAX_TOP = 60
-- Steps between yields while walking a capture. Keeps Studio responsive on a
-- 256-frame capture of a busy session without making a small one slower.
local YIELD_EVERY = 25_000

--[[
	Scopes that are the absence of work. They dominate any ranking by time --
	"Sleep" was 10 s of a 64-frame capture in an idle Studio -- and say nothing.
]]
local IDLE_NAMES = {
	["Sleep"] = true,
	["Wait"] = true,
	["Idle"] = true,
	["WaitForFrame"] = true,
	["WaitForSingleObject"] = true,
	["Yield"] = true,
}

local libmp: any = nil
local loadMs: number? = nil

local function compile(source: string): any
	local ok, chunk = pcall(loadstring :: any, source, "=LibMP")
	if ok and typeof(chunk) == "function" then
		return chunk()
	end
	-- A playtest server disables loadstring; a ModuleScript still compiles.
	local module = Instance.new("ModuleScript")
	module.Name = "LibMP"
	local settable = pcall(function()
		module.Source = source
	end)
	if not settable then
		module:Destroy()
		Dispatch.fail("LIBMP_UNAVAILABLE", "This session can neither loadstring nor set a script's source, so LibMP cannot load here.")
	end
	local required, result = pcall(require, module)
	module:Destroy()
	if not required then
		Dispatch.fail("LIBMP_UNAVAILABLE", string.format("LibMP failed to load: %s", tostring(result)))
	end
	return result
end

local function load(): any
	if libmp ~= nil then
		return libmp
	end
	local started = os.clock()
	local response = Net.request("GET", "/vendor/libmp", nil)
	if not response.ok or #response.body < 1000 then
		Dispatch.fail(
			"LIBMP_UNAVAILABLE",
			string.format("Could not fetch LibMP from the server: %s", tostring(response.error or response.statusCode)),
			"Update the MCP server; LibMP ships with it from 1.0.5."
		)
	end
	local loaded = compile(response.body)
	if typeof(loaded) ~= "table" or loaded.Control == nil then
		Dispatch.fail("LIBMP_UNAVAILABLE", "LibMP loaded but did not return its module table.")
	end
	if not loaded.Control:IsBackendReady() then
		Dispatch.fail(
			"LIBMP_UNAVAILABLE",
			"MicroProfilerService is not reachable or its data format is newer than this LibMP.",
			"Update the MCP server to get a newer LibMP."
		)
	end
	libmp = loaded
	loadMs = math.round((os.clock() - started) * 1000)
	return loaded
end

-- " RBX Worker C" and " RBX Worker K" are one pool; ranking them apart splits
-- one hot job into a dozen small-looking rows.
local function threadClass(name: string): string
	local trimmed = string.match(name, "^%s*(.-)%s*$") or name
	local pool = string.match(trimmed, "^(RBX Worker) %a$")
	if pool then
		return pool
	end
	pool = string.match(trimmed, "^(HttpClientHandler::worker)")
	return pool or trimmed
end

local function percentile(sorted: { number }, p: number): number
	if #sorted == 0 then
		return 0
	end
	local index = math.clamp(math.ceil(#sorted * p), 1, #sorted)
	return sorted[index]
end

local function round(value: number): number
	return math.round(value * 1000) / 1000
end

type Row = {
	thread: string,
	timer: number,
	total: number,
	self: number,
	calls: number,
	perFrame: { [number]: number },
}

function MicroProfiler.capture(params: { [string]: any }): { [string]: any }
	local firstLoad = libmp == nil
	local LibMP = load()
	local control = LibMP.Control

	local frames = math.clamp(math.floor(tonumber(params.frames) or DEFAULT_FRAMES), 4, MAX_FRAMES)
	local top = math.clamp(math.floor(tonumber(params.top) or DEFAULT_TOP), 1, MAX_TOP)
	local filter = if typeof(params.filter) == "string" and params.filter ~= "" then string.lower(params.filter) else nil
	local threadFilter = if typeof(params.thread) == "string" and params.thread ~= "" then string.lower(params.thread) else nil
	local includeIdle = params.includeIdle == true
	local sortBy = if params.sort == "total" then "total" else "self"

	control:SetFrameLimit(frames)
	control:EnableProfiler(true)
	control:EnableCapture(true)

	-- The profiler records a rolling window, so a capture is the last `frames`
	-- frames. Waiting long enough to fill it at 60 FPS (plus slack) is the only
	-- wait needed; `seconds` lets a caller hold it open across a known spike.
	local wait = tonumber(params.seconds) or (frames / 60 + 0.5)
	task.wait(math.clamp(wait, 0.2, 30))

	local captured = control:CaptureToBufferSync()
	if params.keepRunning ~= true then
		control:EnableProfiler(false)
	end
	if captured == nil then
		Dispatch.fail("NO_CAPTURE", "The MicroProfiler returned no capture.", "Try again; the first capture after enabling can be empty.")
	end

	local session = LibMP.Session.OpenFromBuffer(captured)
	if not session or not session:IsValid() then
		if session then
			session:Dispose()
		end
		Dispatch.fail("NO_CAPTURE", "The capture could not be opened.")
	end

	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		local global = session:FetchGlobalDesc()
		local tick = global.TickToMsCpu
		local frameMin, frameMax = session:GetFrameIdMin(), session:GetFrameIdMax()
		if frameMin == 0 and frameMax == 0 then
			Dispatch.fail("NO_CAPTURE", "The capture holds no frames yet.", "Capture again after a second.")
		end

		-- Frame times from the CPU frame boundaries.
		local frameMs: { [number]: number } = {}
		local frameList: { number } = {}
		for frameId = frameMin, frameMax do
			local desc = session:FetchFrameDesc(frameId)
			if desc and not desc.IsPaused then
				local ms = (desc.TickEndCpu - desc.TickStartCpu) * tick
				if ms > 0 then
					frameMs[frameId] = ms
					table.insert(frameList, ms)
				end
			end
		end
		local sortedFrames = table.clone(frameList)
		table.sort(sortedFrames)
		local worstFrame, worstMs = 0, -1
		for frameId, ms in frameMs do
			if ms > worstMs then
				worstFrame, worstMs = frameId, ms
			end
		end
		local sum = 0
		for _, ms in frameList do
			sum += ms
		end

		-- Thread names, and which threads to walk.
		local threadName: { [number]: string } = {}
		local threadIds: { number } = {}
		local threadCount = 0
		for _, id in session:FetchThreadIds() do
			local desc = session:FetchThreadDesc(id)
			if not desc.IsGpu then
				threadCount += 1
				local class = threadClass(desc.ThreadName)
				threadName[id] = class
				if threadFilter == nil or string.find(string.lower(desc.ThreadName), threadFilter, 1, true) then
					table.insert(threadIds, id)
				end
			end
		end
		if #threadIds == 0 then
			Dispatch.fail("NOT_FOUND", string.format("No CPU thread matches %q.", tostring(params.thread)), 'Main thread is "RBX Main"; workers are "RBX Worker".')
		end

		local iterator = session:CreateLogIterator()
		iterator:Configure({
			ThreadIds = threadIds,
			SkipGpuThreads = true,
			SkipEvents = true,
			SkipPausedFrames = true,
		})
		local state = iterator:GetState()

		local rows: { [string]: Row } = {}
		local kids: { [number]: { [number]: number } } = {}
		local steps = 0
		while iterator:Step() do
			steps += 1
			if steps % YIELD_EVERY == 0 then
				task.wait()
			end
			if state:IsExit() and not state:ThreadStackIsUnderflowed() then
				local level = state:ThreadStackDepth()
				local element = iterator:GetCurrentThreadStackElement(level)
				if element then
					local thread = state:ThreadId()
					local duration = math.max(0, (state:Timestamp() - element:EnterTimestampFrameLocal()) * tick)
					local children = kids[thread]
					if children == nil then
						children = {}
						kids[thread] = children
					end
					local self = math.max(0, duration - (children[level] or 0))
					children[level] = 0
					if level > 0 then
						children[level - 1] = (children[level - 1] or 0) + duration
					end

					local timer = state:TimerId()
					local class = threadName[thread] or "?"
					local key = class .. "\0" .. timer
					local row = rows[key]
					if row == nil then
						row = { thread = class, timer = timer, total = 0, self = 0, calls = 0, perFrame = {} }
						rows[key] = row
					end
					row.total += duration
					row.self += self
					row.calls += 1
					local frameId = state:FrameId()
					row.perFrame[frameId] = (row.perFrame[frameId] or 0) + duration
				end
			end
		end
		iterator:Dispose()

		-- Names, filters, ranking.
		local timerCache: { [number]: { name: string, group: string } } = {}
		local groupCache: { [number]: string } = {}
		local function describe(timer: number)
			local cached = timerCache[timer]
			if cached then
				return cached
			end
			local desc = session:FetchTimerDesc(timer)
			local group = groupCache[desc.GroupId]
			if group == nil then
				group = session:FetchGroupDesc(desc.GroupId).GroupName
				groupCache[desc.GroupId] = group
			end
			cached = { name = desc.TimerName, group = group :: string }
			timerCache[timer] = cached
			return cached
		end

		local frameCount = math.max(1, #frameList)
		local ranked = {}
		local idleMs = 0
		for _, row in rows do
			local info = describe(row.timer)
			if IDLE_NAMES[info.name] and not includeIdle then
				idleMs += row.self
				continue
			end
			if filter ~= nil
				and not string.find(string.lower(info.name), filter, 1, true)
				and not string.find(string.lower(info.group), filter, 1, true)
			then
				continue
			end
			local peak, peakFrame = 0, 0
			for frameId, ms in row.perFrame do
				if ms > peak then
					peak, peakFrame = ms, frameId
				end
			end
			table.insert(ranked, {
				thread = row.thread,
				group = info.group,
				name = info.name,
				selfMs = round(row.self),
				totalMs = round(row.total),
				avgMs = round(row.total / frameCount),
				peakMs = round(peak),
				peakFrame = peakFrame,
				calls = row.calls,
				worst = row.perFrame[worstFrame],
			})
		end
		table.sort(ranked, function(a, b)
			if sortBy == "total" then
				return a.totalMs > b.totalMs
			end
			return a.selfMs > b.selfMs
		end)

		-- What filled the worst frame, so a spike names its cause directly.
		local worstScopes = {}
		for _, entry in ranked do
			if entry.worst and entry.worst > 0 then
				table.insert(worstScopes, entry)
			end
		end
		table.sort(worstScopes, function(a, b)
			return a.worst > b.worst
		end)
		local worstList = {}
		for i = 1, math.min(8, #worstScopes) do
			local entry = worstScopes[i]
			table.insert(worstList, {
				thread = entry.thread,
				name = entry.group .. "/" .. entry.name,
				ms = round(entry.worst),
			})
		end

		local scopes = {}
		for i = 1, math.min(top, #ranked) do
			local entry = ranked[i]
			entry.worst = nil
			table.insert(scopes, entry)
		end

		local export: string? = nil
		if params.export == true then
			local okExport, html = pcall(function()
				return LibMP.Tools:ConvertToBuffer(session, LibMP.Enums.ContainerFormat.CompressedHtml)
			end)
			if okExport and html ~= nil then
				export = buffer.tostring(html)
			end
		end

		return {
			frames = #frameList,
			frameRange = { frameMin, frameMax },
			threads = threadCount,
			walkedThreads = #threadIds,
			steps = steps,
			captureBytes = buffer.len(captured),
			frameMs = {
				avg = round(sum / frameCount),
				p50 = round(percentile(sortedFrames, 0.5)),
				p95 = round(percentile(sortedFrames, 0.95)),
				max = round(math.max(worstMs, 0)),
				worstFrame = worstFrame,
			},
			idleMs = round(idleMs),
			sort = sortBy,
			scopes = scopes,
			matched = #ranked,
			worstFrameScopes = worstList,
			html = export,
			exportFailed = if params.export == true and export == nil then true else nil,
			libmpLoadMs = if firstLoad then loadMs else nil,
			profilerLeftOn = params.keepRunning == true,
		}
	end)
	session:Dispose()
	if not ok then
		error(result, 0)
	end
	return result
end

return MicroProfiler

local Polaris = script:FindFirstAncestor("Polaris")
local App = Polaris.App
local Components = App.Components
local Util = Components.Util

local Fusion = require(Polaris.Packages.Fusion)

local Theme = require(App.Theme)
local animate = require(Util.animate)
local getState = require(Util.getState)
local stripProps = require(Util.stripProps)

local Container = require(Components.Container)
local Padding = require(Components.Padding)
local Corner = require(Components.Corner)
local Glyph = require(Components.Glyph)
local List = require(Components.List)
local Text = require(Components.Text)
local Box = require(Components.Box)

local New = Fusion.New
local Value = Fusion.Value
local Tween = Fusion.Tween
local Spring = Fusion.Spring
local Hydrate = Fusion.Hydrate
local OnEvent = Fusion.OnEvent
local Computed = Fusion.Computed
local Children = Fusion.Children
local OnChange = Fusion.OnChange
local peek = Fusion.peek

local COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS = {
	"Title",
	"Color",
	"Expanded",
	"Elements",
}

type Props = {
	Title: string,
	Color: Fusion.CanBeState<Color3>?,
	Expanded: boolean?,
	Elements: { Instance },
}

return function(props: Props): Frame
	local isExpanded = Value(props.Expanded or false)
	local absoluteSize = Value(Vector2.zero)

	local isHovered = Value(false)
	local isPressed = Value(false)

	local state = getState({
		Hovered = isHovered,
		Pressed = isPressed,
	})

	local color = animate(
		Computed(function(use)
			return use(isExpanded) and use(Theme.Colors.ActiveBackground) or use(Theme.Colors.Background)
		end),
		state
	)

	return Hydrate(Box {
		ClipsDescendants = Computed(function(use)
			return not use(isExpanded)
		end),
		AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.None,
		Size = Spring(
			Computed(function(use)
				return UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Theme.CompSizeY.Large + (use(isExpanded) and use(absoluteSize).Y or 0))
			end),
			30
		),
		[Children] = {
			New "TextButton" {
				Text = "",
				AutoButtonColor = false,
				Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Theme.CompSizeY.Large),
				BackgroundColor3 = color,
				[OnEvent "InputBegan"] = function(input)
					if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement then
						isHovered:set(true)
					elseif input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then
						isPressed:set(true)
					end
				end,
				[OnEvent "InputEnded"] = function(input)
					if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement then
						isHovered:set(false)
					elseif input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then
						isPressed:set(false)
					end
				end,
				[OnEvent "Activated"] = function()
					isExpanded:set(not peek(isExpanded))
				end,
				[Children] = {
					Corner {},
					Container {
						Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1),
						[Children] = {
							Padding {},
							Text {
								Text = props.Title,
								FontFace = Theme.Fonts.Bold,
								TextSize = Theme.TextSize.Large,
								TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left,
								Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1),
								Color = props.Color or Theme.Colors.Text,
							},
							Glyph {
								AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0.5),
								Position = UDim2.fromScale(1, 0.5),
								Size = UDim2.fromOffset(16, 16),
								Glyph = "ChevronDown",
								Color = props.Color or Theme.Colors.Text,
								Rotation = Spring(
									Computed(function(use)
										return use(isExpanded) and 180 or 0
									end),
									30
								),
							},
						},
					},
					New "Frame" {
						AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 1),
						Position = UDim2.fromScale(0, 1),
						Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 0.2),
						BackgroundColor3 = color,
						BorderSizePixel = 0,
						BackgroundTransparency = Tween(
							Computed(function(use)
								return use(isExpanded) and 0 or 1
							end),
							TweenInfo.new(0.15, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut)
						),
					},
				},
			},
			Container {
				Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 0),
				Position = UDim2.fromOffset(0, Theme.CompSizeY.Large),
				[OnChange "AbsoluteSize"] = function(size)
					absoluteSize:set(size)
				end,
				[Children] = {
					List {
						Spacing = 0,
					},
					props.Elements,
				},
			},
		},
	})(stripProps(props, COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS))
end

--!strict
--[[
	Carries console activity from a playtest's SERVER view to its CLIENT view.

	Pressing Play gives this plugin three lives: the editor's, the playtest
	server's, and the playtest client's. Studio shows whichever belongs to the
	view you are looking at, and it defaults to the client -- which is the one
	life that can do nothing. Roblox forbids HTTP from a client session, so that
	panel has no way to see the bridge, and it sat on a standby notice while the
	agent worked a few feet away in a view the user was not looking at.

	The two DataModels share no memory, no globals and no services. The only
	channel between them is the game's own replication, so that is what this
	uses: the server plugin puts a RemoteEvent in ReplicatedStorage and fires
	each console event across it; the client plugin listens and replays them
	into its own console. The prism reacts, the log fills, and the view the user
	actually has open stops lying about what is happening.

	The cost is honest and worth stating: this plugin writes one instance into
	the running game. It is `Archivable = false` so it can never be saved with
	the place, it exists only while a playtest is running, and it goes when the
	playtest's DataModel does. Nothing reads it but the client half of this
	plugin, and nothing is sent up from the client -- the traffic is one-way, so
	a game's own scripts cannot use it to reach the editor.
]]

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

--[[
	Named to be recognised in the Explorer rather than to be hidden.

	Someone will see this appear in ReplicatedStorage mid-playtest and want to
	know what put it there; a cryptic name turns that into a hunt. The prefix is
	unlikely enough to collide with a real game's instances.
]]
local CHANNEL = "__rbxStudioMcpMirror"

local Mirror = {}

local remote: RemoteEvent? = nil

--[[
	Held shut until the server session has finished introducing itself.

	Both halves of a playtest log their own banner, place and status, so a
	channel that is open from the start delivers the server's copy of all of it
	to a client that has already written its own -- the panel comes up saying
	"rbx-studio v0.3.6" and "place: Game" twice, a line apart, which reads as a
	glitch because it is one.

	Opened on the server's "connected" row rather than after a fixed wait: that
	is the exact point where its startup ends and the session's real activity
	begins, and everything after it is news the client does not already have.
]]
local open = false

function Mirror.open()
	open = true
end

--[[
	True only in the half of a playtest that can reach the bridge.

	`IsRunning` separates a playtest from the editor, and `IsServer` separates
	the two halves of it. The editor session must not do any of this: it has no
	playtest to mirror and writing to its ReplicatedStorage would put the
	instance in the user's actual place.
]]
function Mirror.isPlaytestServer(): boolean
	return RunService:IsRunning() and RunService:IsServer()
end

function Mirror.isPlaytestClient(): boolean
	return RunService:IsRunning() and RunService:IsClient()
end

--[[
	Opens the channel from the playtest server.

	A leftover from an earlier test in the same DataModel is replaced rather
	than reused: reusing one whose connections are gone looks like a working
	channel that silently delivers nothing.
]]
function Mirror.startServer()
	if not Mirror.isPlaytestServer() then
		return
	end
	local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(CHANNEL)
	if existing ~= nil then
		existing:Destroy()
	end
	local event = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	event.Name = CHANNEL
	-- Never saved with the place, whatever the user does while the test runs.
	event.Archivable = false
	event.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	remote = event
end

--[[
	Sends one console event, and never fails loudly.

	This is decoration on top of the console. A replication error here must not
	take down the call it was reporting on, so every send is guarded and a dead
	channel simply stops mirroring.
]]
function Mirror.send(kind: string, arguments: { any })
	local event = remote
	if event == nil or not open then
		return
	end
	pcall(function()
		event:FireAllClients(kind, arguments)
	end)
end

--[[
	Listens on the playtest client.

	`WaitForChild` with a timeout rather than an indefinite wait: if the server
	half never opens the channel the client should go quiet, not hang a thread
	for the length of the playtest.
]]
function Mirror.startClient(onMessage: (string, { any }) -> ())
	if not Mirror.isPlaytestClient() then
		return
	end
	task.spawn(function()
		local event = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild(CHANNEL, 30)
		if event == nil or not event:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
			return
		end
		event.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(kind, arguments)
			-- Shape-checked because anything on the wire can be forged by a
			-- script in the place being tested. Nothing here is trusted enough
			-- to index without looking.
			if typeof(kind) == "string" and typeof(arguments) == "table" then
				onMessage(kind, arguments :: { any })
			end
		end)
	end)
end

return Mirror

--!strict
--[[
	Thin HttpService wrapper.

	Plugins reach 127.0.0.1 through a per-plugin permission grant rather than the
	experience-wide "Allow HTTP Requests" setting, so the first request after
	install pops a permission dialog. That failure mode is turned into a message
	the user can act on instead of a raw Luau error.
]]

local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")

local Config = require(script.Parent.Config)

local Net = {}

export type Response = {
	ok: boolean,
	statusCode: number,
	body: string,
	error: string?,
}

--[[
	Performs a request and never throws. Callers branch on `ok`; `error` carries
	a user-facing explanation when the request could not be made at all.
]]
function Net.request(method: string, path: string, body: string?): Response
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return HttpService:RequestAsync({
			Url = Config.baseUrl() .. path,
			Method = method,
			Headers = Config.headers(),
			Body = body,
		})
	end)

	if not ok then
		return {
			ok = false,
			statusCode = 0,
			body = "",
			error = Net.explain(tostring(result)),
		}
	end

	local response = result :: any
	if response.Success then
		return {
			ok = true,
			statusCode = response.StatusCode,
			body = response.Body,
		}
	end

	--[[
		The request reached the bridge and it refused -- every `send()` on that
		side answers with `{ error: "..." }`, and that string is the actual reason
		(missing header, protocol mismatch, no Studio connected). Falling back to
		a bare status code discarded it and showed "handshake failed" instead,
		which is accurate about nothing. Decoded defensively: a body that is not
		JSON, or JSON without an `error` field, still gets a readable fallback.
	]]
	local decoded = Net.decode(response.Body)
	local reason = if typeof(decoded) == "table" and typeof((decoded :: any).error) == "string"
		then (decoded :: any).error
		else string.format("server responded %d", response.StatusCode)

	return {
		ok = false,
		statusCode = response.StatusCode,
		body = response.Body,
		error = reason,
	}
end

function Net.postJson(path: string, value: any): Response
	return Net.request("POST", path, HttpService:JSONEncode(value))
end

--[[
	Turns HttpService's terse errors into something the user can act on. These
	strings surface in the plugin widget, so they are written for a person, not
	for the agent.
]]
function Net.explain(message: string): string
	local lowered = string.lower(message)

	if string.find(lowered, "not enabled") or string.find(lowered, "permission") then
		return "Studio blocked the request. Open Plugins -> Manage Plugins, find "
			.. "Studio MCP, and allow it to reach 127.0.0.1."
	end
	if
		string.find(lowered, "connectfail")
		or string.find(lowered, "curl")
		or string.find(lowered, "could not connect")
		or string.find(lowered, "connection refused")
	then
		return string.format(
			"Nothing is listening on port %d. Start the server with "
				.. "`npx -y @el4cteo/rbx-studio-mcp` (or check --port if you changed it).",
			Config.getPort()
		)
	end
	if string.find(lowered, "timedout") or string.find(lowered, "timeout") then
		return "The server stopped responding. It may have been restarted; "
			.. "the plugin will keep retrying."
	end
	return message
end

--[[
	Decodes a JSON body, returning nil rather than throwing on malformed input.
	A truncated frame is a transport hiccup, not a reason to kill the plugin.
]]
function Net.decode(body: string): any?
	local ok, value = pcall(HttpService.JSONDecode, HttpService, body)
	if not ok then
		return nil
	end
	return value
end

return Net

--!strict
--[[
	The panel's themes: a colour set and the animated background that goes
	with it. One is active at a time; `Console.applyTheme` repaints the panel
	when it changes, and the choice is saved by init.server.
]]

export type Palette = {
	background: Color3,
	surface: Color3,
	rule: Color3,
	text: Color3,
	dim: Color3,
	green: Color3,
	red: Color3,
	amber: Color3,
	cyan: Color3,
	violet: Color3,
}

export type Theme = {
	id: string,
	label: string,
	-- One line for the picker.
	blurb: string,
	palette: Palette,
	-- The far end of the background gradient, and the input boxes' fill.
	deep: Color3,
	-- Which animated background it uses; see Backdrop.
	backdrop: string,
	-- The colour its dot in the header shows.
	accent: Color3,
}

local rgb = Color3.fromRGB

local function freeze(theme: Theme): Theme
	table.freeze(theme.palette)
	return table.freeze(theme) :: any
end

local THEMES: { Theme } = {
	freeze({
		id = "nebula",
		label = "Nebula",
		blurb = "navy, light-blue lines, a drifting constellation",
		backdrop = "constellation",
		accent = rgb(124, 196, 255),
		deep = rgb(6, 23, 51),
		palette = {
			background = rgb(18, 59, 122),
			surface = rgb(6, 23, 51),
			rule = rgb(120, 190, 255),
			text = rgb(232, 241, 255),
			dim = rgb(150, 176, 214),
			green = rgb(95, 227, 161),
			red = rgb(255, 125, 140),
			amber = rgb(251, 191, 36),
			cyan = rgb(124, 196, 255),
			violet = rgb(185, 162, 255),
		},
	}),
	freeze({
		id = "ember",
		label = "Ember",
		blurb = "charcoal and deep red, sparks rising",
		backdrop = "embers",
		accent = rgb(255, 140, 66),
		deep = rgb(14, 9, 9),
		palette = {
			background = rgb(58, 22, 18),
			surface = rgb(20, 12, 11),
			rule = rgb(255, 140, 66),
			text = rgb(250, 236, 228),
			dim = rgb(196, 160, 146),
			green = rgb(140, 220, 130),
			red = rgb(255, 98, 98),
			amber = rgb(255, 196, 92),
			cyan = rgb(255, 170, 110),
			violet = rgb(240, 150, 190),
		},
	}),
	freeze({
		id = "tide",
		label = "Tide",
		blurb = "deep teal, slow rolling waves",
		backdrop = "waves",
		accent = rgb(70, 220, 190),
		deep = rgb(3, 24, 28),
		palette = {
			background = rgb(10, 66, 72),
			surface = rgb(4, 28, 32),
			rule = rgb(90, 220, 200),
			text = rgb(226, 248, 244),
			dim = rgb(142, 190, 184),
			green = rgb(110, 236, 170),
			red = rgb(255, 128, 128),
			amber = rgb(250, 204, 92),
			cyan = rgb(110, 226, 236),
			violet = rgb(170, 176, 255),
		},
	}),
	freeze({
		id = "galaxy",
		label = "Galaxy",
		blurb = "deep indigo, a turning spiral under an analysis overlay",
		backdrop = "galaxy",
		accent = rgb(110, 200, 255),
		deep = rgb(4, 6, 20),
		palette = {
			background = rgb(18, 26, 70),
			surface = rgb(7, 10, 28),
			rule = rgb(110, 200, 255),
			text = rgb(230, 240, 255),
			dim = rgb(140, 160, 205),
			green = rgb(120, 240, 200),
			red = rgb(255, 110, 140),
			amber = rgb(255, 214, 130),
			cyan = rgb(110, 210, 255),
			violet = rgb(180, 160, 255),
		},
	}),
	freeze({
		id = "aurora",
		label = "Aurora",
		blurb = "midnight purple under a curtain of northern lights",
		backdrop = "aurora",
		accent = rgb(150, 255, 200),
		deep = rgb(9, 6, 24),
		palette = {
			background = rgb(34, 20, 72),
			surface = rgb(12, 8, 30),
			rule = rgb(170, 150, 255),
			text = rgb(240, 236, 255),
			dim = rgb(170, 160, 210),
			green = rgb(130, 250, 190),
			red = rgb(255, 120, 150),
			amber = rgb(255, 210, 120),
			cyan = rgb(120, 220, 255),
			violet = rgb(200, 160, 255),
		},
	}),
	freeze({
		id = "monolith",
		label = "Monolith",
		blurb = "greyscale slabs, drifting dust, a passing beam",
		backdrop = "sweep",
		accent = rgb(200, 200, 200),
		deep = rgb(10, 10, 11),
		palette = {
			background = rgb(34, 34, 36),
			surface = rgb(16, 16, 17),
			rule = rgb(190, 190, 194),
			text = rgb(238, 238, 240),
			dim = rgb(150, 150, 156),
			green = rgb(200, 200, 204),
			red = rgb(255, 120, 120),
			amber = rgb(220, 220, 220),
			cyan = rgb(210, 210, 214),
			violet = rgb(176, 176, 182),
		},
	}),
}

local byId: { [string]: Theme } = {}
for _, theme in THEMES do
	byId[theme.id] = theme
end
-- Galaxy replaced Circuit; a saved "circuit" lands on it.
byId.circuit = byId.galaxy

local active: Theme = THEMES[1]

local Palette = {}

-- Interface type; the log's timestamps and durations stay monospaced.
Palette.FONT = Enum.Font.BuilderSans
Palette.FONT_MEDIUM = Enum.Font.BuilderSansMedium
Palette.FONT_BOLD = Enum.Font.BuilderSansBold

function Palette.get(): Palette
	return active.palette
end

function Palette.deep(): Color3
	return active.deep
end

function Palette.theme(): Theme
	return active
end

function Palette.list(): { Theme }
	return THEMES
end

function Palette.find(id: string): Theme?
	return byId[string.lower(id)]
end

-- Makes `id` the active theme. False when it is unknown or already active.
function Palette.use(id: string): boolean
	local theme = byId[string.lower(id)]
	if theme == nil or theme == active then
		return false
	end
	active = theme
	return true
end

return Palette
