local Polaris = script:FindFirstAncestor("Polaris")
local App = Polaris.App
local Components = App.Components
local Util = Components.Util

local Fusion = require(Polaris.Packages.Fusion)

local GlobalUtil = require(Polaris.Util)

local Theme = require(App.Theme)
local animate = require(Util.animate)
local stripProps = require(Util.stripProps)
local getTextSize = require(Util.getTextSize)
local getState = require(Util.getState)
local isState = require(Util.isState)

local Container = require(Components.Container)
local Padding = require(Components.Padding)
local Corner = require(Components.Corner)
local Glyph = require(Components.Glyph)
local Input = require(Components.Input)
local List = require(Components.List)
local Box = require(Components.Box)

local New = Fusion.New
local Ref = Fusion.Ref
local Value = Fusion.Value
local Spring = Fusion.Spring
local Hydrate = Fusion.Hydrate
local OnEvent = Fusion.OnEvent
local Cleanup = Fusion.Cleanup
local Computed = Fusion.Computed
local Children = Fusion.Children
local Observer = Fusion.Observer
local ForValues = Fusion.ForValues
local cleanup = Fusion.cleanup
local peek = Fusion.peek

local BUTTON_COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS = {
	"Activated",
	"IsSelected",
	"IsDimmed",
	"IsFirst",
	"IsLast",
}

type ButtonProps = {
	Activated: () -> (),
	IsSelected: Fusion.Computed<boolean>,
	IsDimmed: Fusion.Computed<boolean>,
	IsFirst: Fusion.Value<boolean>?,
	IsLast: boolean,
	[any]: any,
}

local function Button(props: ButtonProps): TextButton
	local isHovered = Value(false)
	local isPressed = Value(false)

	local state = getState({
		Hovered = isHovered,
		Pressed = isPressed,
	})
	local lastState = peek(state)

	local color = animate(
		Computed(function(use)
			return use(props.IsSelected) and use(Theme.Colors.Brand) or use(Theme.Colors.Background)
		end),
		state
	)

	-- Hide very minor hover flicker of the first button when the dropdown is expanded
	local disconnect = Observer(state):onChange(function()
		if props.IsFirst and not peek(props.IsFirst) then
			local state = peek(state)

			if state == Enum.GuiState.Idle and lastState == Enum.GuiState.Press then
				task.defer(function()
					if peek(props.IsFirst) then
						color:setPosition(
							peek(props.IsSelected) and peek(Theme.Colors.Brand) or peek(Theme.Colors.Background)
						)
					end
				end)
			end

			lastState = state
		end
	end)

	return Hydrate(New "TextButton" {
		Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Theme.CompSizeY.Medium),
		FontFace = Theme.Fonts.Regular,
		AutoButtonColor = false,
		TextSize = Theme.TextSize.Large,
		TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left,
		BackgroundColor3 = color,
		TextColor3 = Computed(function(use)
			return use(props.IsSelected) and use(Theme.Colors.TextBranded)
				or use(props.IsDimmed) and use(Theme.Colors.TextDimmed)
				or use(Theme.Colors.Text)
		end),
		[OnEvent "InputBegan"] = function(input)
			if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement then
				isHovered:set(true)
			elseif input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then
				isPressed:set(true)
			end
		end,
		[OnEvent "InputEnded"] = function(input)
			if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement then
				isHovered:set(false)
			elseif input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then
				isPressed:set(false)
			end
		end,
		[OnEvent "Activated"] = function()
			if props.IsFirst then
				isHovered:set(false)
				isPressed:set(false)
			end

			props.Activated()
		end,
		[Cleanup] = disconnect,
		[Children] = GlobalUtil.join(
			{
				Padding {
					Horizontal = 6,
				},
			},
			if props.IsFirst
				then {
					Corner {},
					New "Frame" {
						AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1),
						Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 1),
						Size = UDim2.fromScale(1.2, 0.2),
						BackgroundColor3 = color,
						BorderSizePixel = 0,
						Visible = Computed(function(use)
							return use(props.IsFirst)
						end),
					},
				}
				elseif props.IsLast then {
					Corner {},
					New "Frame" {
						AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0),
						Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0),
						Size = UDim2.fromScale(1.2, 0.2),
						BackgroundColor3 = color,
						BorderSizePixel = 0,
					},
				}
				else {}
		),
	})(stripProps(props, BUTTON_COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS))
end

local COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS = {
	"Selected",
	"Options",
	"Value",
	"Placeholder",
}

type Props = {
	Selected: ((option: string) -> ())?,
	Options: { string },
	Value: Fusion.CanBeState<string>?,
	Placeholder: Fusion.CanBeState<string>?,
	[any]: any,
}

return function(props: Props): TextButton
	local value = isState(props.Value) and props.Value or Value(props.Value or props.Options[1])
	local placeholder = isState(props.Placeholder) and props.Placeholder or Value(props.Placeholder or props.Options[1])

	local isOpen = Value(false)
	local anchor = Value(0)
	local ref = Value(nil)

	local size
	do
		local maxSize = Vector2.zero

		for _, option in props.Options do
			local textSize = getTextSize(option)

			if textSize.X > maxSize.X then
				maxSize = textSize
			end
		end

		size = UDim2.fromOffset(maxSize.X + 40, Theme.CompSizeY.Medium)
	end

	return Hydrate(Container {
		AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.None,
		Size = size,
		[Children] = {
			Padding {
				Horizontal = 6,
			},
			Glyph {
				AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0.5),
				Position = UDim2.fromScale(1, 0.5),
				Size = UDim2.fromOffset(16, 16),
				Glyph = "ChevronDown",
				Color = Theme.Colors.Text,
				ZIndex = 2,
				Transparency = Computed(function(use)
					return use(isOpen) and 1 or 0
				end),
			},
			Input {
				Finished = function()
					task.delay(0.1, function()
						isOpen:set(false)
					end)
				end,
				[Ref] = ref,
			},
			Box {
				ClipsDescendants = true,
				AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.None,
				Size = Spring(
					Computed(function(use)
						return UDim2.new(1, 12, use(isOpen) and #props.Options or 1, 0)
					end),
					40
				),
				AnchorPoint = Computed(function(use)
					if use(isOpen) then
						local index = table.find(props.Options, peek(value))
						anchor:set((index - 1) / #props.Options)
					end

					return Vector2.new(0.5, peek(anchor))
				end),
				Position = Computed(function(use)
					return UDim2.fromScale(0.5, use(isOpen) and 0 or use(anchor))
				end),
				[Children] = {
					Container {
						Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, #props.Options),
						[Children] = {
							List {
								Spacing = 0,
							},
							ForValues(props.Options, function(_, option)
								local isFirst = option == props.Options[1]

								return Button {
									Text = Computed(function(use)
										if isFirst then
											return use(isOpen) and option or use(value)
										else
											return option
										end
									end),
									IsSelected = Computed(function(use)
										return use(isOpen) and use(value) == option
									end),
									IsDimmed = Computed(function(use)
										return not use(isOpen) and use(value) ~= use(placeholder)
									end),
									Activated = function()
										local open = peek(isOpen)
										isOpen:set(not open)

										if not open then
											peek(ref):CaptureFocus()
										end

										if not open or option == peek(value) then
											return
										end

										value:set(option)

										if props.Selected then
											props.Selected(option)
										end
									end,
									IsFirst = isFirst and isOpen or nil,
									IsLast = option == props.Options[#props.Options],
								}
							end, cleanup),
						},
					},
				},
			},
		},
	})(stripProps(props, COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS))
end

local fs = require("@std/fs")
local json = require("@std/json")
local path = require("@std/path")
local query = require("@std/syntax/query")
local syntax = require("@std/syntax")
local utils = require("@std/syntax/utils")

type Side = "server" | "client" | "shared"
type InstancePath = { string }
type Sourcemap = { byFile: { [string]: InstancePath }, instances: { [string]: boolean } }
type Scope = { script: InstancePath, values: { [any]: any }, seen: { [any]: boolean } }

local name = "require_boundaries"

local SIDES: { [string]: Side } = {
	ServerScriptService = "server",
	ServerStorage = "server",
	StarterPlayer = "client",
	StarterGui = "client",
	ReplicatedFirst = "client",
	ReplicatedStorage = "shared",
	Workspace = "shared",
}

local MAY_REQUIRE: { [Side]: { [Side]: boolean } } = {
	server = { server = true, shared = true },
	client = { client = true, shared = true },
	shared = { shared = true },
}

local sourcemaps: { [string]: Sourcemap } = {}

local function loadSourcemap(file: string): Sourcemap
	local absolute = path.format(path.resolve(file))
	if sourcemaps[absolute] then
		return sourcemaps[absolute]
	end
	local result: Sourcemap = { byFile = {}, instances = {} }
	local function walk(node: any, at: InstancePath)
		result.instances[table.concat(at, ".")] = true
		for _, filePath in node.filePaths or {} do
			result.byFile[path.format(path.resolve(path.dirname(absolute), filePath))] = at
		end
		for _, child in node.children or {} do
			local childAt = table.clone(at)
			table.insert(childAt, child.name)
			walk(child, childAt)
		end
	end
	walk(json.deserialize(fs.readFileToString(absolute)), {})
	sourcemaps[absolute] = result
	return result
end

-- The instance path an expression names, or nil when it isn't static.
local function resolve(expr: any, scope: Scope): InstancePath?
	if expr.tag == "group" then
		return resolve(expr.expression, scope)
	elseif expr.tag == "global" then
		if expr.name.text == "game" then
			return {}
		elseif expr.name.text == "script" then
			return table.clone(scope.script)
		end
	elseif expr.tag == "local" then
		local value = scope.values[expr["local"]]
		if value and not scope.seen[value] then
			scope.seen[value] = true
			return resolve(value, scope)
		end
	elseif expr.tag == "indexname" and expr.accessor.text == "." then
		local parent = resolve(expr.expression, scope)
		if parent and expr.index.text == "Parent" then
			return if #parent > 0 then { table.unpack(parent, 1, #parent - 1) } else nil
		elseif parent then
			table.insert(parent, expr.index.text)
			return parent
		end
	elseif expr.tag == "index" and expr.index.tag == "string" then
		local parent = resolve(expr.expression, scope)
		if parent then
			table.insert(parent, expr.index.token.text)
			return parent
		end
	elseif expr.tag == "call" and expr.self then
		local argument = expr.arguments[1]
		local child = argument and argument.node.tag == "string" and argument.node.token.text
		local receiver = child and resolve(expr.func.expression, scope)
		local method = expr.func.index.text
		if receiver and method == "GetService" and #receiver == 0 then
			return { child }
		elseif receiver and (method == "WaitForChild" or method == "FindFirstChild") then
			table.insert(receiver, child)
			return receiver
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- The side and feature of an instance, where the feature is the child of the deepest feature root.
local function locate(at: InstancePath, featureRoots: { string }): (Side?, string?)
	local joined = table.concat(at, ".")
	local deepest = 0
	for _, root in featureRoots do
		local depth = #string.split(root, ".")
		if depth > deepest and string.sub(joined, 1, #root + 1) == root .. "." then
			deepest = depth
		end
	end
	return SIDES[at[1]], if deepest > 0 then at[deepest + 1] else nil
end

local function lint(ast: syntax.AstStatBlock, sourcepath: path.Path?, context: any)
	local options = context.options
	local sourcemap = loadSourcemap(options.sourcemap or "sourcemap.json")
	local script = sourcepath and sourcemap.byFile[path.format(path.resolve(sourcepath))]
	if script == nil then
		return {}
	end
	local featureRoots = options.featureRoots or {}
	local helpers = {}
	for _, feature in options.sharedFeatures or {} do
		helpers[feature] = true
	end
	local fromSide, fromFeature = locate(script, featureRoots)

	local values = {}
	query.findAllFromRoot(ast, utils.isStatLocal):forEach(function(stat: any)
		if #stat.variables == 1 and #stat.values == 1 then
			values[stat.variables[1].node] = stat.values[1].node
		end
	end)

	local violations = {}
	query.findAllFromRoot(ast, utils.isRequireCall):forEach(function(call: any)
		local argument = call.arguments[1]
		local target = argument and resolve(argument.node, { script = script, values = values, seen = {} })
		if target == nil then
			return
		end
		local targetName = table.concat(target, ".")
		local toSide, toFeature = locate(target, featureRoots)
		local message
		if not sourcemap.instances[targetName] then
			message = `{targetName} is not in the sourcemap`
		elseif fromSide and toSide and not MAY_REQUIRE[fromSide][toSide] then
			message = `{fromSide} code requires {toSide} code: {targetName}`
		elseif fromFeature and toFeature and fromFeature ~= toFeature and not helpers[toFeature] then
			message = `feature {fromFeature} requires feature {toFeature}: {targetName}`
		end
		if message then
			table.insert(violations, {
				lintname = name,
				location = call.location,
				message = message,
				severity = "error",
				sourcepath = sourcepath,
			})
		end
	end)
	return violations
end

return table.freeze({ name = name, lint = lint })

--!strict
--[[
	Dot-notation instance paths, e.g. "Workspace.Map.Spawn".

	Paths are the address format for every tool, so resolution failures are the
	most common error an agent will hit. Each failure says which segment broke
	and what does exist at that level, which is usually enough for the model to
	fix the path itself instead of falling back to a blind tree dump.
]]

local Dispatch = require(script.Parent.Dispatch)
local Handles = require(script.Parent.Handles)

local Paths = {}
Paths.handle = Handles.of
Paths.stableId = Handles.id

--[[
	Splits a path into segments. A leading "game." is optional and stripped, so
	both "game.Workspace.Part" and "Workspace.Part" resolve identically.
]]
function Paths.split(path: string): { string }
	local segments: { string } = {}
	for segment in string.gmatch(path, "[^%.]+") do
		table.insert(segments, segment)
	end
	if segments[1] == "game" then
		table.remove(segments, 1)
	end
	return segments
end

--[[
	Splits "Part[3]" into ("Part", 3), or ("Part", nil) when unindexed.

	Sibling names are not unique in Roblox -- a Workspace with 77 parts all named
	"Part" is completely ordinary -- so a bare dotted path is ambiguous and
	`FindFirstChild` would silently pick the first match. Every path this module
	emits therefore carries a 1-based index whenever the name is shared, and
	`resolve` honours it.
]]
local function parseSegment(segment: string): (string, number?)
	local name, index = string.match(segment, "^(.*)%[(%d+)%]$")
	if name and index then
		return name, tonumber(index)
	end
	return segment, nil
end

export type NameIndex = { [Instance]: { [string]: { Instance } } }

--[[
	Groups a parent's children by name, memoised across one request. Without the
	memo, formatting paths for N same-named siblings is O(N^2); a listing of a
	few thousand parts would stall Studio's main thread.
]]
local function childrenByName(parent: Instance, memo: NameIndex?): { [string]: { Instance } }
	local cached = if memo then memo[parent] else nil
	if cached then
		return cached
	end

	local byName: { [string]: { Instance } } = {}
	for _, child in parent:GetChildren() do
		local list = byName[child.Name]
		if not list then
			list = {}
			byName[child.Name] = list
		end
		table.insert(list, child)
	end

	--[[
		Same-named siblings put into a fixed order.

		`GetChildren` does not return a stable order (see `stableOrder` in
		Discover), so `Part[2]` could name a different part on the call that
		reads the path back than on the one that printed it. The engine's debug
		id is fixed for an instance's lifetime, which makes it the tiebreak.

		Guarded, because this module also runs in the client relay, where
		`GetDebugId` is not callable. That VM assigns stable in-memory ids instead,
		so repeated reads retain their order without changing the place.
	]]
	for _, list in byName do
		if #list > 1 then
			local ids: { [Instance]: string } = {}
			for _, child in list do
				local ok, id = pcall(function()
					return child:GetDebugId()
				end)
				ids[child] = if ok then id else string.format("%012d", Handles.id(child))
			end
			table.sort(list, function(a: Instance, b: Instance): boolean
				return ids[a] < ids[b]
			end)
		end
	end

	if memo then
		memo[parent] = byName
	end
	return byName
end

--[[
	1-based position among identically named siblings, or nil when the name is
	already unique and no index is needed.
]]
local function siblingIndex(instance: Instance, memo: NameIndex?): number?
	local parent = instance.Parent
	if not parent then
		return nil
	end

	local list = childrenByName(parent, memo)[instance.Name]
	if not list or #list <= 1 then
		return nil
	end
	for index, child in list do
		if child == instance then
			return index
		end
	end
	return nil
end

--[[
	Names a parent's children for an error message, collapsing repeats.

	Same-named siblings are ordinary in Roblox, and listing them one by one spent
	the whole budget saying "Part, Part, Part" 25 times -- which tells a reader
	nothing and hides the names that would have helped. Repeats are counted
	instead, and the count is exactly what says an index is needed.
]]
local function childNames(parent: Instance, limit: number): string
	local order: { string } = {}
	local counts: { [string]: number } = {}
	for _, child in parent:GetChildren() do
		if counts[child.Name] == nil then
			counts[child.Name] = 0
			table.insert(order, child.Name)
		end
		counts[child.Name] += 1
	end

	if #order == 0 then
		return "(no children)"
	end

	local names: { string } = {}
	for _, name in order do
		if #names >= limit then
			table.insert(names, string.format("... %d more", #order - limit))
			break
		end
		local count = counts[name]
		table.insert(names, if count > 1 then string.format("%s (x%d)", name, count) else name)
	end
	return table.concat(names, ", ")
end

--[[
	Finds one child by a single segment, honouring "Name[2]" and, at the root,
	fetching services by class name -- they are not always present as children
	until first accessed.

	The second return is a diagnostic for the one miss a caller cannot work out
	from the sibling list: an index past the end of a name that does exist.
]]
local function childBySegment(
	parent: Instance,
	segment: string,
	atRoot: boolean
): (Instance?, string?)
	local name, ordinal = parseSegment(segment)

	if ordinal then
		local list = childrenByName(parent, nil)[name]
		local child = if list then list[ordinal] else nil
		if child then
			return child, nil
		end
		-- Not an index after all: a child literally named "x[1]". Typed by hand,
		-- or from a path emitted before `Paths.of` began marking such names.
		local literal = parent:FindFirstChild(segment)
		if literal then
			return literal, nil
		end
		if list == nil then
			return nil, nil
		end
		return nil,
			string.format(
				'"%s" has %d child%s named "%s", so [%d] is past the end. Indexes are '
					.. "1-based and shift when siblings are added or removed -- read a "
					.. "fresh path from `find` or `tree`.",
				parent:GetFullName(),
				#list,
				if #list == 1 then "" else "ren",
				name,
				ordinal
			)
	end

	if atRoot then
		local ok, service = pcall(function()
			return game:GetService(name :: any)
		end)
		if ok and service then
			return service, nil
		end
	end
	local found = parent:FindFirstChild(name)
	if found == nil then
		return nil, nil
	end
	--[[
		A bare name shared by several siblings is ambiguous. For a READ the
		first match is a harmless answer and stays accepted. For a WRITE it is
		refused (see Dispatch.strictPaths): it used to resolve to whichever came
		first, so `modify` on "Map.Door" changed one door of two without a word.
		The refusal names the indexed paths, which every path this module emits
		already carries.
	]]
	-- Only writes pay for the scan; reads never look past the first match.
	local count = 0
	if Dispatch.strictPaths() then
		for _, child in parent:GetChildren() do
			if child.Name == name then
				count += 1
				if count > 1 then
					break
				end
			end
		end
	end
	if count > 1 then
		local total = #(childrenByName(parent, nil)[name] or {})
		return nil,
			string.format(
				'"%s" has %d children named "%s", so the path is ambiguous. Pick one: %s[1] .. %s[%d] '
					.. "(`find` or `tree` shows which is which).",
				parent:GetFullName(),
				total,
				name,
				name,
				name,
				total
			)
	end
	return found, nil
end

--[[
	Resolves a path to an Instance, or raises a NOT_FOUND with the failing
	segment and its siblings. `FindFirstChild` is used rather than indexing so a
	missing child never throws a bare Luau error.

	Instance names may contain dots -- "Dr. Simon" is an ordinary name, and so is
	"v1.2 backup" -- while the separator is a dot too, so such a name arrives
	here already split into pieces. Each step therefore tries consuming one
	segment first and rejoins further segments only if that leads nowhere, which
	means the search has to BACK TRACK: with both "Dr" and "Dr. Who" present,
	"Workspace.Dr. Who.Head" matches "Dr", fails to find " Who" under it, and
	must return to try "Dr. Who". A first pass without that backtracking left the
	tools emitting `Workspace.Dr. Who` as a path and then refusing to read it
	back, which is worse than either behaviour on its own.

	Shortest-first keeps the old precedence: where a short name resolves the
	whole remaining path, it still wins over a longer join.
]]
function Paths.resolve(path: string): Instance
	if typeof(path) == "string" and string.sub(path, 1, 5) == "@mcp:" then
		return Handles.resolve(path)
	end
	if typeof(path) ~= "string" or path == "" then
		Dispatch.fail(
			"BAD_PATH",
			"An instance path is required.",
			'Paths are dot-separated from the DataModel root, e.g. "Workspace.Map.Spawn". '
				.. "Use `find` or `tree` to discover valid paths."
		)
	end

	local segments = Paths.split(path)
	if #segments == 0 then
		return game
	end

	-- The deepest point any branch of the search reached, so a failure still
	-- reports the segment that actually broke rather than the first one tried.
	local deepest = 0
	local deepestParent: Instance = game
	local deepestNote: string? = nil
	-- The segment text the note is about: with a rejoined name it is not
	-- `segments[failedAt]`, and reporting that instead named "Mr" for a path
	-- that asked for "Mr. X[3]".
	local deepestSegment: string? = nil

	local function walk(current: Instance, index: number): Instance?
		if index > #segments then
			return current
		end
		if index - 1 > deepest then
			deepest = index - 1
			deepestParent = current
			deepestNote = nil
			deepestSegment = nil
		end

		for last = index, #segments do
			local joined = table.concat(segments, ".", index, last)
			local child, note = childBySegment(current, joined, index == 1)
			if note and index - 1 == deepest then
				deepestNote = note
				deepestSegment = joined
			end
			if child then
				local found = walk(child, last + 1)
				if found then
					return found
				end
			end
		end
		return nil
	end

	local resolved = walk(game, 1)
	if resolved then
		return resolved
	end

	local failedAt = deepest + 1
	if deepestNote and string.find(deepestNote, "the path is ambiguous", 1, true) then
		return Dispatch.fail(
			"AMBIGUOUS_PATH",
			string.format('"%s" matches more than one instance.', table.concat(segments, ".", 1, failedAt)),
			deepestNote
		)
	end
	local reached = if deepest > 0 then table.concat(segments, ".", 1, deepest) .. "." else ""
	local named = if deepestSegment
		then reached .. deepestSegment
		else table.concat(segments, ".", 1, failedAt)
	return Dispatch.fail(
		"NOT_FOUND",
		string.format('No instance at "%s".', named),
		if deepestNote
			then deepestNote
			else string.format(
				'"%s" has no child named "%s". It does have: %s',
				deepestParent:GetFullName(),
				segments[failedAt],
				childNames(deepestParent, 25)
			)
	)
end

--[[
	Resolves many paths at once, collecting failures instead of stopping at the
	first one. Batch tools report every bad path in a single response so the
	agent can fix them all in one retry rather than one call per mistake.
]]
function Paths.resolveMany(paths: { string }): ({ Instance }, { string })
	local resolved: { Instance } = {}
	local failures: { string } = {}
	for _, path in paths do
		local ok, result = pcall(Paths.resolve, path)
		if ok then
			table.insert(resolved, result :: Instance)
		else
			local err = result :: any
			table.insert(
				failures,
				string.format("%s: %s", path, if typeof(err) == "table" then err.message else tostring(err))
			)
		end
	end
	return resolved, failures
end

--[[
	Formats an instance into a path that resolves back to that exact instance.

	`GetFullName` is deliberately not used: it emits "Workspace.Part" for every
	one of 77 parts named "Part", so the paths it produces are not addresses at
	all. Here each segment gains a [n] suffix when its name is shared with a
	sibling.

	Pass a shared `memo` when formatting many instances in one request.

	The index is positional, so it shifts if same-named siblings are inserted or
	removed between calls. Read a fresh path after any structural change.
]]
--[[
	The position among same-named siblings, or nil when the name is unique --
	the `n` in `Name[n]`. Exposed for `sync`, which names files after it.
]]
function Paths.ordinal(instance: Instance, memo: NameIndex?): number?
	return siblingIndex(instance, memo)
end

function Paths.of(instance: Instance, memo: NameIndex?): string
	--[[
		Refuses anything that is not an Instance, rather than duck-typing it.

		This walks `.Name` and `.Parent`, which a plain table can also have -- so
		handed a table carrying those two fields it used to return a perfectly
		well-formed path for an object that exists nowhere in the data model.
		That happened: `GeometryService:FragmentAsync` returns `{Index, Instance}`
		wrappers, a handler assigned `.Name` and `.Parent` to the wrapper, and
		this function reported eight new parts by full path when none had been
		created. A fabricated path is worse than an error, because everything
		downstream treats it as real.
	]]
	if typeof(instance) ~= "Instance" then
		error(
			string.format(
				"Paths.of expects an Instance, got %s. This is a bug in the caller, "
					.. "not in the request.",
				typeof(instance)
			),
			2
		)
	end

	if instance == game then
		return "game"
	end

	local segments: { string } = {}
	local current: Instance? = instance

	while current ~= nil and current ~= game do
		local node = current :: Instance
		local ordinal = siblingIndex(node, memo)
		-- A name that itself ends in "[n]" would read back as an index into a
		-- shorter name. An explicit index keeps it literal: "x[1][1]".
		if ordinal == nil and string.match(node.Name, "%[%d+%]$") then
			ordinal = 1
		end
		table.insert(
			segments,
			1,
			if ordinal then string.format("%s[%d]", node.Name, ordinal) else node.Name
		)
		current = node.Parent
	end

	return table.concat(segments, ".")
end

return Paths

local Polaris = script:FindFirstAncestor("Polaris")
local App = Polaris.App
local Components = App.Components
local Util = Components.Util

local Fusion = require(Polaris.Packages.Fusion)

local Theme = require(App.Theme)
local stripProps = require(Util.stripProps)

local New = Fusion.New
local Hydrate = Fusion.Hydrate
local Children = Fusion.Children

-- Polaris draws its own icons on a 16x16 canvas from frames and strokes, so the
-- interface carries no inherited bitmaps and stays sharp at any scale.
local BASE = 16

local COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS = {
	"Glyph",
	"Color",
	"Transparency",
	"Thickness",
	"Scale",
}

type Props = {
	Glyph: string?,
	Color: Fusion.CanBeState<Color3>?,
	Transparency: Fusion.CanBeState<number>?,
	Thickness: number?,
	Scale: number?,
	[any]: any,
}

return function(props: Props): Frame
	local color = props.Color or Theme.Colors.Text
	local transparency = props.Transparency or 0
	local thickness = props.Thickness or 1.6

	local function bar(width: number, height: number, x: number, y: number, rotation: number?): Frame
		return New "Frame" {
			AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
			Position = UDim2.fromOffset(x, y),
			Size = UDim2.fromOffset(width, height),
			Rotation = rotation or 0,
			BackgroundColor3 = color,
			BackgroundTransparency = transparency,
			BorderSizePixel = 0,
			[Children] = {
				New "UICorner" { CornerRadius = UDim.new(1, 0) },
			},
		}
	end

	local function dot(size: number, x: number, y: number): Frame
		return New "Frame" {
			AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
			Position = UDim2.fromOffset(x, y),
			Size = UDim2.fromOffset(size, size),
			BackgroundColor3 = color,
			BackgroundTransparency = transparency,
			BorderSizePixel = 0,
			[Children] = {
				New "UICorner" { CornerRadius = UDim.new(1, 0) },
			},
		}
	end

	local function ring(diameter: number): Frame
		return New "Frame" {
			AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
			Position = UDim2.fromOffset(BASE / 2, BASE / 2),
			Size = UDim2.fromOffset(diameter, diameter),
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			[Children] = {
				New "UICorner" { CornerRadius = UDim.new(1, 0) },
				New "UIStroke" {
					Thickness = thickness,
					Color = color,
					Transparency = transparency,
					ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border,
				},
			},
		}
	end

	local function glyphLabel(text: string, textSize: number): TextLabel
		return New "TextLabel" {
			AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
			Position = UDim2.fromOffset(BASE / 2, BASE / 2),
			Size = UDim2.fromOffset(BASE, textSize * 1.5),
			BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			BorderSizePixel = 0,
			Text = text,
			TextSize = textSize,
			FontFace = Theme.Fonts.Bold,
			TextColor3 = color,
			TextTransparency = transparency,
		}
	end

	local builders = {}

	-- Gear: a ring with radial teeth and a hub
	function builders.Settings()
		local children = { ring(8.5) }

		for i = 1, 6 do
			local angle = (i - 1) * math.pi / 3

			table.insert(
				children,
				bar(3, 1.6, BASE / 2 + math.cos(angle) * 5.4, BASE / 2 + math.sin(angle) * 5.4, math.deg(angle))
			)
		end

		table.insert(children, dot(2.6, BASE / 2, BASE / 2))

		return children
	end

	-- Info: ring with a lower case i
	function builders.Info()
		return {
			ring(12),
			dot(2.2, BASE / 2, 5),
			bar(2.2, 5, BASE / 2, 10),
		}
	end

	-- Help: ring with a question mark (plain ASCII, no font gamble)
	function builders.Help()
		return {
			ring(12.5),
			glyphLabel("?", 9),
		}
	end

	-- Check: two strokes
	function builders.Check()
		return {
			bar(4.4, 2.2, 6.2, 9.6, 45),
			bar(8.6, 2.2, 9.8, 7.2, -50),
		}
	end

	-- Chevrons: two strokes forming a V
	function builders.ChevronDown()
		return {
			bar(5.4, 2, 5.8, 8.6, 38),
			bar(5.4, 2, 10.2, 8.6, -38),
		}
	end

	function builders.ChevronRight()
		return builders.ChevronDown()
	end

	-- External: arrow leaving towards the top right
	function builders.External()
		return {
			bar(9.4, 2, 7.4, 8.6, -45),
			bar(4.6, 2, 10.6, 3.4, 0),
			bar(2, 4.6, 12.6, 5.4, 0),
		}
	end

	local children = {
		New "UIScale" { Scale = props.Scale or 1 },
	}

	if props.Glyph and builders[props.Glyph] then
		for _, child in builders[props.Glyph]() do
			table.insert(children, child)
		end
	end

	return Hydrate(New "Frame" {
		Name = "Glyph",
		AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(BASE, BASE),
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		BorderSizePixel = 0,
		Rotation = if props.Glyph == "ChevronRight" then 90 else 0,
		[Children] = children,
	})(stripProps(props, COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS))
end

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local roblox = require("@lune/roblox")

local db = roblox.getReflectionDatabase()
local game = roblox.deserializePlace(fs.readFile(process.args[1]))

local function propertiesOf(className)
	local names = {}
	local class = db:GetClass(className)
	while class do
		for name, property in class.Properties do
			if not table.find(property.Tags, "NotScriptable") and not table.find(property.Tags, "ReadOnly") and not table.find(property.Tags, "Deprecated") and not table.find(property.Tags, "Hidden") then
				table.insert(names, name)
			end
		end
		class = class.Superclass and db:GetClass(class.Superclass)
	end
	table.sort(names)
	return names
end

local lines = {}
local function visit(instance, path)
	local okDefault, default = pcall(roblox.Instance.new, instance.ClassName)
	table.insert(lines, path .. " (" .. instance.ClassName .. ")")
	for _, name in propertiesOf(instance.ClassName) do
		local ok, value = pcall(function() return instance[name] end)
		local same = okDefault and pcall(function() return default[name] end) and default[name] == value
		if ok and not same and name ~= "Name" and name ~= "Parent" then
			table.insert(lines, "  " .. name .. " = " .. tostring(value))
		end
	end
	local children = instance:GetChildren()
	table.sort(children, function(a, b) return a.Name < b.Name end)
	for _, child in children do
		visit(child, path .. "/" .. child.Name)
	end
end
local services = game:GetChildren()
table.sort(services, function(a, b) return a.Name < b.Name end)
for _, service in services do visit(service, service.Name) end
fs.writeFile(process.args[2], table.concat(lines, "\n") .. "\n")

--!strict
-- The same guarded Stats read in plugin and client VMs.
local Stats = game:GetService("Stats")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local Perf = {}
local function round(value: number, places: number): number
	local scale = 10 ^ places
	return math.floor(value * scale + 0.5) / scale
end

--[[
	Reads a Stats property without assuming it exists. The set has changed across
	engine versions, and one missing counter should not fail the whole snapshot.
]]
local function stat(name: string): number?
	local ok, value = pcall(function()
		return (Stats :: any)[name]
	end)
	if ok and typeof(value) == "number" then
		return value
	end
	return nil
end

local function millis(name: string): number?
	local seconds = stat(name)
	return if seconds then round(seconds * 1000, 3) else nil
end

local function flag(name: string): boolean?
	local ok, value = pcall(function()
		return (Stats :: any)[name]
	end)
	if ok and typeof(value) == "boolean" then
		return value
	end
	return nil
end

local function rounded(name: string, places: number): number?
	local value = stat(name)
	return if value then round(value, places) else nil
end

function Perf.snapshot(): { [string]: any }
	--[[
		Read one tag at a time, not with `GetMemoryUsageMbAllCategories`.

		The aggregate call is the obvious one and is closed to us: it now requires
		the InternalTest capability, so from a plugin it only ever raises "the
		current thread cannot call 'GetMemoryUsageMbAllCategories'". Measured, not
		assumed -- and the same refusal comes back in an editor session and in a
		playtest, so there is no context in which waiting for it pays off.

		`GetMemoryUsageMbForTag` carries no such restriction, and walking
		`Enum.DeveloperMemoryTag` reaches every category the Developer Console's
		Memory tab shows. Zero-valued tags are dropped so the list stays readable.
	]]
	local memory: { { [string]: any } } = {}
	local memoryProblem: string? = nil

	for _, tag in Enum.DeveloperMemoryTag:GetEnumItems() do
		local ok, value = pcall(function()
			return Stats:GetMemoryUsageMbForTag(tag)
		end)
		if not ok then
			-- One refusal means the whole route is shut, not that this tag is
			-- special; stop rather than repeat the same failure for every item.
			memoryProblem = string.format("Stats refused the call: %s", tostring(value))
			break
		end
		if typeof(value) == "number" and value > 0 then
			table.insert(memory, { category = tag.Name, megabytes = round(value, 2) })
		end
	end

	table.sort(memory, function(a, b)
		return a.megabytes > b.megabytes
	end)

	local okTotal, total = pcall(function()
		return Stats:GetTotalMemoryUsageMb()
	end)

	--[[
		A playtest server has no renderer, so every drawing counter reads zero --
		zero draw calls, zero triangles, no frame time. Left unexplained that is
		the most flattering possible misreading of a place's performance, so the
		snapshot says outright that those numbers are absent rather than good.
	]]
	local headless = RunService:IsRunning() and RunService:IsServer() and not RunService:IsClient()

	return {
		renderless = headless or nil,
		frame = {
			frameTimeMs = millis("FrameTime"),
			heartbeatTimeMs = millis("HeartbeatTime"),
			physicsStepTimeMs = millis("PhysicsStepTime"),
			renderCpuMs = millis("RenderCPUFrameTime"),
			renderGpuMs = millis("RenderGPUFrameTime"),
		},
		scene = {
			instances = stat("InstanceCount"),
			parts = stat("PrimitivesCount"),
			movingParts = stat("MovingPrimitivesCount"),
			contacts = stat("ContactsCount"),
			drawcalls = stat("SceneDrawcallCount"),
			triangles = stat("SceneTriangleCount"),
		},
		network = {
			receiveKbps = rounded("DataReceiveKbps", 1),
			sendKbps = rounded("DataSendKbps", 1),
		},
		memory = {
			totalMb = if okTotal and typeof(total) == "number" then round(total, 1) else nil,
			-- Studio only accumulates the per-category breakdown while this is on,
			-- so an empty list means "not measured" rather than "nothing used".
			trackingEnabled = flag("MemoryTrackingEnabled"),
			categories = memory,
			problem = if #memory == 0 then memoryProblem else nil,
		},
	}
end

return Perf

local Children = Fusion.Children

local COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS = {
	"Activated",
	"Solid",
	"Icon",
	"Glyph",
	"GlyphColor",
	"BackgroundActive",
	"Blending",
}

type Props = {
	Activated: (() -> ())?,
	Solid: Fusion.CanBeState<boolean>?,
	Icon: Fusion.CanBeState<string>?,
	Glyph: string?,
	GlyphColor: Fusion.CanBeState<Color3>?,
	BackgroundActive: Fusion.Computed<boolean>?,
	Blending: boolean?,
	[any]: any,
}

return function(props: Props): TextButton
	local isHovered = Value(false)
	local isPressed = Value(false)

	local state = getState({
		Hovered = isHovered,
		Pressed = isPressed,
	})

	local color = animate(
		Computed(function(use)
			return if use(props.Solid)
				then use(Theme.Colors.Brand)
				else use(props.BackgroundActive) and use(Theme.Colors.ActiveBackground) or use(
					Theme.Colors.Background
				)
		end),
		state
	)

	return Hydrate(New "TextButton" {
		Size = UDim2.fromOffset(Theme.CompSizeY.Large, Theme.CompSizeY.Large),
		Text = "",
		AutoButtonColor = false,
		BackgroundColor3 = color,
		[OnEvent "InputBegan"] = function(inputObject)
			if inputObject.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement then
				isHovered:set(true)
			elseif inputObject.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then
				isPressed:set(true)
			end
		end,
		[OnEvent "InputEnded"] = function(inputObject)
			if inputObject.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement then
				isHovered:set(false)
			elseif inputObject.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then
				isPressed:set(false)
			end
		end,
		[OnEvent "Activated"] = function()
			if props.Activated then
				props.Activated()
			end
		end,
		[Children] = {
			Border {},
			props.Glyph and Glyph {
				AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
				Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5),
				Scale = 1.15,
				Glyph = props.Glyph,
				Color = props.GlyphColor or Computed(function(use)
					return use(props.Solid) and use(Theme.Colors.TextBranded) or use(Theme.Colors.Text)
				end),
			} or Image {
				AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
				Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5),
				Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.55, 0.55),
				SizeConstraint = Enum.SizeConstraint.RelativeYY,
				ImageTransparency = default(props.Blending, true) and Computed(function(use)
					return use(Theme.IsDark) and 0.1 or 0.2
				end) or 0,
				ImageColor3 = Computed(function(use)
					return use(props.Solid) and use(Theme.Colors.TextBranded) or use(Theme.Colors.Text)
				end),
				Image = props.Icon,
			},
		},
	})(stripProps(props, COMPONENT_ONLY_PROPS))
end

--!strict
--[[
	Turns a command into something a person can read at a glance.

	The console used to print the wire name: `-> script.edit`, `-> instances.create`.
	That tells you the plugin is alive and nothing else. Watching an agent work,
	the interesting question is always "what is it touching" -- and the answer is
	sitting right there in the parameters, one field away from being shown.

	So `script.edit` on ServerScriptService.KillBrick becomes "Edit KillBrick",
	and `instances.create` with eight children becomes "Create 8 instances in
	Workspace". The subject is what the user recognises; the op is what the
	protocol needed.

	Three rules hold this together:

	  Name the subject, not the path. "KillBrick" is what someone called their
	  script; "ServerScriptService.Systems.KillBrick" is where it lives, and it
	  buries the recognisable part behind the part that never changes.

	  Count when there are several. "Edit 4 scripts" is worth reading. Listing
	  four paths in a 76-pixel-wide log line is not.

	  Never invent. An unknown op falls back to a tidied version of its own name
	  rather than a guess, because a console that lies about what ran is worse
	  than one that reads awkwardly.
]]

local Phrase = {}

-- The tail of a dotted path is the bit a human named. Everything before it is
-- Roblox's filing system.
local function leaf(path: any): string?
	if typeof(path) ~= "string" or path == "" then
		return nil
	end
	local last = string.match(path, "([^%.]+)$")
	if last == nil or last == "" then
		return nil
	end
	-- Array indexing survives into the name -- "Part[3]" is meaningfully
	-- different from "Part" when there are several siblings.
	return last
end

local function count(value: any): number
	if typeof(value) ~= "table" then
		return 0
	end
	return #(value :: { any })
end

--[[
	"1 script" / "4 scripts", without the caller assembling it each time.
]]
local function plural(n: number, singular: string, pluralForm: string?): string
	local word = if n == 1 then singular else (pluralForm or (singular .. "s"))
	return string.format("%d %s", n, word)
end

--[[
	Describes a list of paths: the name when there is one, a count when there are
	several. This is the shape most batch tools take.
]]
local function subjectOf(paths: any, noun: string): string
	local total = count(paths)
	if total == 1 then
		local name = leaf((paths :: { any })[1])
		if name ~= nil then
			return name
		end
	end
	if total > 1 then
		return plural(total, noun)
	end
	return noun
end

--[[
	Capitalises an op fragment for the fallback. `snapshots` -> `Snapshots`.
]]
local function titleCase(value: string): string
	return (string.upper(string.sub(value, 1, 1)) .. string.sub(value, 2))
end

type Describer = (params: { [string]: any }) -> string

--[[
	One entry per op. Each reads its own parameters, because what identifies a
	call differs completely between them: a script edit is about a path, a
	playtest is about a mode, a find is about what was searched for.
]]
local DESCRIBERS: { [string]: Describer } = {
	["sync.scan"] = function(params)
		return if params.revisions == false then "Check script layout for sync" else "Scan scripts for sync"
	end,
	["sync.read"] = function(params)
		return "Read " .. subjectOf(params.paths, "script") .. " for sync"
	end,
	["sync.apply"] = function(params)
		local total = count(params.writes) + count(params.creates) + count(params.deletes) + count(params.moves)
		return string.format("Sync %d change%s from files", total, if total == 1 then "" else "s")
	end,
	["sync.shape"] = function()
		return "Check script layout for sync"
	end,
	["sync.revisions"] = function()
		return "Check script revisions"
	end,
	["sync.changes"] = function()
		return "Check for script changes"
	end,
	["sync.stop"] = function()
		return "Stop sync tracking"
	end,
	["sync.log"] = function()
		return "Sync note"
	end,
	["analysis.publish"] = function()
		return "Show Luau check in Script Analysis"
	end,
	["analysis.clear"] = function()
		return "Clear Luau check findings"
	end,
	["sync.classes"] = function(params)
		return "List classes in " .. (leaf(params.path) or "tree")
	end,
	["sync.export"] = function(params)
		return "Export " .. (leaf(params.path) or "tree") .. " to a build file"
	end,
	["sync.build"] = function(params)
		local spec = params.spec
		local name = if typeof(spec) == "table" then spec.name or spec.className else nil
		return "Build " .. tostring(name or "tree") .. " from a build file"
	end,
	["script.read"] = function(params)
		return "Read " .. subjectOf(params.paths, "script")
	end,
	["script.edit"] = function(params)
		local edits = params.edits
		local total = count(edits)
		if total == 1 then
			local name = leaf((edits :: { any })[1].path)
			if name ~= nil then
				return "Edit " .. name
			end
		end
		-- Several edits often land on one script, and "Edit 3 scripts" would be
		-- wrong when it is three changes to one file.
		local seen: { [string]: boolean } = {}
		local distinct = 0
		for _, edit in (edits or {}) :: { { [string]: any } } do
			local name = leaf(edit.path)
			if name ~= nil and not seen[name] then
				seen[name] = true
				distinct += 1
			end
		end
		if distinct == 1 then
			for name in seen do
				return string.format("Edit %s (%s)", name, plural(total, "change"))
			end
		end
		return string.format("Edit %s", plural(distinct, "script"))
	end,
	["script.create"] = function(params)
		local scripts = params.scripts
		if count(scripts) == 1 then
			local one = (scripts :: { any })[1]
			local className = if typeof(one.className) == "string" then one.className else "Script"
			return string.format("Create %s %s", one.name or "script", className)
		end
		return "Create " .. plural(count(scripts), "script")
	end,
	["script.grep"] = function(params)
		local pattern = if typeof(params.pattern) == "string" then params.pattern else "?"
		return string.format('Search scripts for "%s"', pattern)
	end,

	--[[
		Names the class, not just whatever the caller happened to call the
		thing. "Create MainMenu in StarterGui" was true and useless -- a name is
		whatever someone typed, and it says nothing about what actually landed
		in the place. `className` is required by the tool itself, so it is
		always there; the chosen name rides along in quotes when it was given,
		the way script.grep already quotes a search term.
	]]
	["instances.create"] = function(params)
		local instances = params.instances
		local total = count(instances)
		if total == 1 then
			local one = (instances :: { any })[1]
			local className = if typeof(one.className) == "string" and one.className ~= ""
				then one.className
				else "instance"
			local subject = if typeof(one.name) == "string" and one.name ~= ""
				then string.format('%s "%s"', className, one.name)
				else className
			local where = leaf(one.parent)
			return if where ~= nil
				then string.format("Create %s in %s", subject, where)
				else "Create " .. subject
		end
		local where = if total > 0 then leaf((instances :: { any })[1].parent) else nil
		return if where ~= nil
			then string.format("Create %s in %s", plural(total, "instance"), where)
			else "Create " .. plural(total, "instance")
	end,
	["instances.modify"] = function(params)
		local targets = params.targets
		-- Each target carries its own path list, so the honest count is the
		-- total across them rather than the number of entries.
		local total = 0
		local onlyName: string? = nil
		--[[
			Which properties/attributes actually changed, not just how many
			instances did. "Modify Sword" said something happened and nothing
			about what; a caller watching for "did the color change" had no way
			to tell this apart from a rename or an attribute flip.
		]]
		local fields: { string } = {}
		local seenFields: { [string]: boolean } = {}
		local function noteFields(bag: any)
			if typeof(bag) ~= "table" then
				return
			end
			for key in bag :: { [string]: any } do
				if not seenFields[key] then
					seenFields[key] = true
					table.insert(fields, key)
				end
			end
		end
		for _, target in (targets or {}) :: { { [string]: any } } do
			local paths = count(target.paths)
			total += paths
			if paths >= 1 and onlyName == nil then
				onlyName = leaf((target.paths :: { any })[1])
			end
			noteFields(target.properties)
			noteFields(target.attributes)
		end
		if total == 1 and onlyName ~= nil then
			if #fields == 1 then
				return string.format("Set %s on %s", fields[1], onlyName)
			elseif #fields > 1 then
				return string.format("Modify %s (%s)", onlyName, table.concat(fields, ", "))
			end
			return "Modify " .. onlyName
		end
		if #fields == 1 then
			return string.format("Set %s on %s", fields[1], plural(total, "instance"))
		end
		return "Modify " .. plural(total, "instance")
	end,
	["instances.delete"] = function(params)
		return "Delete " .. subjectOf(params.paths, "instance")
	end,
	["instances.move"] = function(params)
		local items = params.items
		local total = count(items)
		local cloning = total > 0 and (items :: { any })[1].mode == "clone"
		local verb = if cloning then "Clone" else "Move"
		if total == 1 then
			local one = (items :: { any })[1]
			local what = leaf(one.path)
			local where = leaf(one.to)
			-- A rename in the same call changes what actually ends up in the
			-- place; "Clone Sword to Backpack" while it lands as "GoldSword"
			-- described an instance that was never created under that name.
			local rename = if typeof(one.name) == "string" and one.name ~= "" then one.name else nil
			if what ~= nil and where ~= nil then
				local base = string.format("%s %s to %s", verb, what, where)
				return if rename ~= nil then base .. " as " .. rename else base
			end
			if what ~= nil then
				return if rename ~= nil
					then string.format("%s %s as %s", verb, what, rename)
					else verb .. " " .. what
			end
		end
		return string.format("%s %s", verb, plural(total, "instance"))
	end,

	["discover.tree"] = function(params)
		local where = leaf(params.path)
		return if where ~= nil then "Browse " .. where else "Browse the place"
	end,
	["discover.inspect"] = function(params)
		--[[
			`inspect` (no explicit `properties`, not concise detail) and `modify`
			(when setting properties) both probe a class before doing the thing
			the caller actually asked for -- reading the properties that matter
			for it, or typing the values it is about to write. That probe is a
			second, genuine call to this same op, and unmarked it logged
			identically to the read it precedes: two lines reading "Inspect X"
			back to back, indistinguishable from asking twice by mistake.
		]]
		if params.probeOnly == true then
			return "Check the class of " .. subjectOf(params.paths, "instance")
		end
		return "Inspect " .. subjectOf(params.paths, "instance")
	end,
	["discover.find"] = function(params)
		if typeof(params.tag) == "string" and params.tag ~= "" then
			return string.format('Find things tagged "%s"', params.tag)
		end
		if typeof(params.nameContains) == "string" and params.nameContains ~= "" then
			return string.format('Find "%s"', params.nameContains)
		end
		if typeof(params.className) == "string" and params.className ~= "" then
			return string.format("Find every %s", params.className)
		end
		return "Search the place"
	end,

	["debug.set"] = function(params)
		local breakpoints = params.breakpoints
		local total = count(breakpoints)
		if total == 1 then
			local one = (breakpoints :: { any })[1]
			local name = leaf(one.path)
			if name ~= nil then
				return string.format("Break on %s:%s", name, tostring(one.line))
			end
		end
		return "Set " .. plural(total, "breakpoint")
	end,
	["debug.clear"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil then "Clear breakpoints in " .. name else "Clear all breakpoints"
	end,
	["debug.remotes"] = function()
		return "Observe playtest RemoteEvent traffic"
	end,
	["debug.watch"] = function(params)
		return "Watch changes to " .. (leaf(params.path) or "an instance")
	end,
	["debug.collisions"] = function(params)
		return "Watch collisions on " .. (leaf(params.path) or "an instance")
	end,
	["debug.snapshots"] = function()
		return "Read what the breakpoints caught"
	end,
	["debug.exceptions"] = function(params)
		return string.format("Break on errors: %s", tostring(params.mode or "Unhandled"))
	end,

	["perf.console"] = function(params)
		if typeof(params.level) == "string" and params.level ~= "" then
			return string.format("Read the %s log", params.level)
		end
		if typeof(params.pattern) == "string" and params.pattern ~= "" then
			return string.format('Search output for "%s"', params.pattern)
		end
		return "Read the output log"
	end,
	["perf.snapshot"] = function()
		return "Measure performance"
	end,
	["perf.profile"] = function(params)
		return string.format("Profile scripts for %ss", tostring(params.seconds or 5))
	end,
	["perf.microprofile"] = function(params)
		return string.format("Capture %s MicroProfiler frames", tostring(params.frames or 64))
	end,
	["perf.coverage"] = function(params)
		local total = count(params.enable)
		if total > 0 then
			return "Instrument " .. plural(total, "script")
		end
		return "Read line coverage"
	end,

	["playtest.control"] = function(params)
		local op = tostring(params.op or "state")
		--[[
			`stop` ends a test by polling this from the *surviving* session every
			400ms until the teardown settles, sometimes five or six times in two
			seconds. Labelled "Check the playtest" like an agent's own status
			check, that read as unexplained repetition with no `stop` line anywhere
			to explain it -- the actual stop went to the session that is by then
			gone, and its console went with it. This name is why: waiting for the
			teardown it just started, not asking again for no reason.
		]]
		if op == "state" and params.waitingForStop == true then
			return "Wait for the playtest to stop"
		end
		if op == "play" then
			return "Start a playtest"
		elseif op == "run" then
			return "Run the place"
		elseif op == "multiplayer" then
			return string.format("Start a %s test", plural(tonumber(params.players) or 2, "player"))
		elseif op == "addPlayers" then
			return string.format("Add %s to the test", plural(tonumber(params.players) or 1, "player"))
		elseif op == "stop" then
			return "Stop the playtest"
		elseif op == "endTest" then
			return "End the test"
		end
		return "Check the playtest"
	end,

	["exec.run"] = function(params)
		local source = if typeof(params.source) == "string" then params.source else ""

		--[[
			Says what the code is about, not what its first line says.

			This used to show the opening line verbatim, which produced entries
			like "Run: local GenerationService = game:GetServi..." -- a fragment
			of a variable declaration, cut mid-word, telling the reader nothing
			except that some code ran. The declaration is never the point of a
			snippet; it is the setup before it.

			So the services it touches stand in for it. That is the one thing a
			snippet reliably says about itself, it is short, and it is what
			someone glancing at the console actually wants: which part of Studio
			is being poked.
		]]
		local services: { string } = {}
		local seen: { [string]: boolean } = {}
		for name in string.gmatch(source, 'GetService%("([%w_]+)"%)') do
			if not seen[name] then
				seen[name] = true
				table.insert(services, name)
			end
		end

		local lines = 0
		for _ in string.gmatch(source, "[^\r\n]+") do
			lines += 1
		end

		if #services == 1 then
			return "Run Luau on " .. services[1]
		elseif #services == 2 then
			return string.format("Run Luau on %s and %s", services[1], services[2])
		elseif #services > 2 then
			return string.format("Run Luau on %s and %d more", services[1], #services - 1)
		end
		return if lines <= 1 then "Run Luau" else string.format("Run Luau (%d lines)", lines)
	end,

	["viewport.select"] = function(params)
		local total = count(params.paths)
		if total == 0 then
			return "Clear the selection"
		end
		return "Select " .. subjectOf(params.paths, "instance")
	end,
	["viewport.raycast"] = function()
		return "Cast a ray"
	end,
	["viewport.pick"] = function()
		return "Identify the instance at a viewport point"
	end,
	["exec.result"] = function()
		return "Retrieve a retained execution result"
	end,
	["client.read"] = function(params)
		return "Read the playtest client: " .. tostring(params.op)
	end,

	["capture.screenshot"] = function()
		return "Take a screenshot"
	end,
	["capture.playtestId"] = function()
		return "Capture the playtest view"
	end,
	["capture.decode"] = function()
		return "Read back the capture"
	end,

	["viewport.focus"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil then "Look at " .. name else "Move the camera"
	end,
	["viewport.camera"] = function()
		return "Move the camera"
	end,

	["geometry.combine"] = function(params)
		local op = tostring(params.op or "union")
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		local verb = if op == "subtract" then "Cut" elseif op == "intersect" then "Intersect" else "Merge"
		if op == "subtract" and name ~= nil then
			local from = count(params.with)
			return string.format("Cut %s out of %s", plural(from, "shape"), name)
		end
		return if name ~= nil then string.format("%s %s", verb, name) else verb .. " parts"
	end,
	["geometry.fragment"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil
			then string.format("Shatter %s into %s", name, plural(tonumber(params.pieces) or 8, "piece"))
			else "Shatter a part"
	end,

	["assets.insert"] = function(params)
		return string.format("Insert asset %s", tostring(params.assetId or "?"))
	end,

	["world.history"] = function(params)
		local action = tostring(params.action or "status")
		if action == "status" then
			return "Check the undo history"
		end
		local steps = tonumber(params.steps) or 1
		return string.format("%s %s", if action == "undo" then "Undo" else "Redo", plural(steps, "step"))
	end,
	["world.collision"] = function(params)
		local action = tostring(params.action or "list")
		local group = if typeof(params.group) == "string" then params.group else "?"
		if action == "list" then
			return "List collision groups"
		elseif action == "create" then
			return "Create collision group " .. group
		elseif action == "assign" then
			return string.format("Put %s in %s", plural(count(params.paths), "instance"), group)
		elseif action == "remove" then
			return "Remove collision group " .. group
		end
		return string.format("Set %s against %s", group, tostring(params.with or "?"))
	end,

	["geometry.mirror"] = function(params)
		local axis = string.upper(tostring(params.axis or "X"))
		local what = plural(count(params.paths), "instance")
		if params.copy == false then
			return string.format("Flip %s across %s", what, axis)
		end
		return string.format("Mirror %s across %s", what, axis)
	end,

	["spatial.cast"] = function(params)
		local shape = tostring(params.shape or "ray")
		-- A part sweep names the part; it has no `from` unless overridden, and
		-- "Cast a part from ?" read as a broken call.
		if shape == "part" then
			return string.format("Sweep %s", leaf(params.path) or "a part")
		end
		local target = if params.to ~= nil then tostring(params.to) else nil
		if target ~= nil then
			return string.format("Cast a %s at %s", shape, target)
		end
		return string.format("Cast a %s from %s", shape, tostring(params.from or "?"))
	end,
	["spatial.overlap"] = function(params)
		local region = tostring(params.region or "box")
		if region == "part" then
			local name = leaf(params.path)
			return if name ~= nil then "Find what overlaps " .. name else "Find overlapping parts"
		end
		return string.format("Find parts in a %s at %s", region, tostring(params.at or "?"))
	end,

	["audio.wire"] = function(params)
		return string.format("Wire %s to %s", leaf(params.from) or "?", leaf(params.to) or "?")
	end,
	["audio.graph"] = function(params)
		local kind = tostring(params.kind or "world")
		local where = leaf(params.parent)
		if kind == "ui" then
			return "Build a UI sound"
		end
		return if where ~= nil then "Build a sound on " .. where else "Build a world sound"
	end,
	["audio.inspect"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil then "Read the audio graph in " .. name else "Read the audio graph"
	end,
	["audio.speech"] = function(params)
		local lines = if typeof(params.lines) == "table" then #params.lines else 0
		return string.format("Voice %s", plural(lines, "line"))
	end,

	["character.moveTo"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil then "Walk to " .. name else string.format("Walk to %s", tostring(params.to or "?"))
	end,
	["character.act"] = function(params)
		local action = tostring(params.action or "jump")
		return titleCase(action) .. " the character"
	end,
	["character.state"] = function()
		return "Check the character"
	end,

	["studio.status"] = function()
		return "Check Studio"
	end,
	["studio.ping"] = function()
		return "Ping"
	end,
	["input.send"] = function(params)
		local steps = params.steps
		local total = count(steps)
		if total == 1 then
			local step = (steps :: { any })[1]
			local kind = tostring(step.kind or "key")
			if kind == "key" then
				local action = tostring(step.action or "tap")
				local verb = if action == "press" then "Hold" elseif action == "release" then "Release" else "Press"
				return string.format("%s %s", verb, tostring(step.key or "?"))
			elseif kind == "click" then
				return string.format("Click (%s, %s)", tostring(step.x or "?"), tostring(step.y or "?"))
			elseif kind == "move" then
				return "Move the pointer"
			elseif kind == "text" then
				return string.format('Type "%s"', tostring(step.text or ""))
			end
		end
		return "Send " .. plural(total, "input step")
	end,

	["api.describe"] = function(params)
		local className = params.className
		return if typeof(className) == "string" and className ~= ""
			then "Look up " .. className
			else "Look up a class"
	end,
	["api.classes"] = function(params)
		local needle = params.contains
		return if typeof(needle) == "string" and needle ~= ""
			then string.format('Search classes for "%s"', needle)
			else "List classes"
	end,

	["perf.scene"] = function(params)
		local section = params.section
		return if typeof(section) == "string" and section ~= ""
			then "Measure the " .. section
			else "Measure the scene"
	end,

	--[[
		Everything below was added after the first pass over this table, and each
		one spent time showing as the fallback -- "Data set",
		"Terrain fill". That form is honest but says nothing about the subject,
		which is the whole point of this module: the panel is watched to see WHAT
		an agent is touching, and 26 of 72 operations were declining to say.
	]]

	["data.list"] = function(params)
		local store = params.store
		if typeof(store) == "string" and store ~= "" then
			return string.format("List the keys in %s", store)
		end
		return "List the data stores"
	end,
	["data.get"] = function(params)
		return string.format("Read %s from %s", tostring(params.key), tostring(params.store))
	end,
	["data.versions"] = function(params)
		return string.format("Read the history of %s", tostring(params.key))
	end,
	["data.set"] = function(params)
		return string.format("SAVE over %s in %s", tostring(params.key), tostring(params.store))
	end,
	["data.remove"] = function(params)
		return string.format("DELETE %s from %s", tostring(params.key), tostring(params.store))
	end,

	["discover.tags"] = function(params)
		local where = leaf(params.path)
		return if where ~= nil then "List the tags used in " .. where else "List every tag in use"
	end,

	["viewport.ui"] = function()
		return "Check the interface for layout faults"
	end,
	["viewport.uisnap"] = function(params)
		local where = leaf(params.path)
		return if where ~= nil then "Snapshot the interface in " .. where else "Snapshot the interface"
	end,
	["viewport.textbounds"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil then "Measure the text in " .. name else "Measure some text"
	end,

	["perf.audit"] = function()
		return "Look for references that point at nothing"
	end,

	["assets.audio"] = function(params)
		local keyword = params.keyword
		return if typeof(keyword) == "string" and keyword ~= ""
			then string.format('Search audio for "%s"', keyword)
			else "Search the audio library"
	end,
	["assets.peek"] = function(params)
		return string.format("Look inside asset %s without inserting it", tostring(params.assetId))
	end,
	["assets.bake"] = function(params)
		return "Bake " .. subjectOf(params.paths, "instance")
	end,

	["character.path"] = function(params)
		local target = leaf(params.toPath)
		return if target ~= nil then "Check the route to " .. target else "Check a route"
	end,

	["device.network"] = function(params)
		local preset = params.preset
		return if typeof(preset) == "string" and preset ~= ""
			then string.format("Simulate a %s connection", preset)
			else "Shape the network connection"
	end,

	["geometry.sweep"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil then "Sweep the path of " .. name else "Sweep a motion volume"
	end,
	["geometry.mesh"] = function(params)
		return "Read the geometry of " .. subjectOf(params.paths, "mesh")
	end,

	["generate.model"] = function(params)
		local prompt = params.prompt
		return if typeof(prompt) == "string" and prompt ~= ""
			then string.format('Generate a model: "%s"', prompt)
			else "Generate a model"
	end,
	["generate.segment"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil then "Cut " .. name .. " into named parts" else "Segment a mesh"
	end,

	["script.open"] = function(params)
		local name = leaf(params.path)
		return if name ~= nil then "Open " .. name .. " in the editor" else "Open a script"
	end,

	["terrain.fill"] = function(params)
		--[[
			The material lives inside the shapes, not beside them.

			Written first against a top-level `material`, which this op has never
			taken, so it always fell through to the bare "Fill terrain" -- seen in
			the panel for a call that laid 50 voxels of sand. The parameters a
			describer reads have to be the ones the handler reads.
		]]
		local shapes = params.shapes
		if typeof(shapes) == "table" and #(shapes :: { any }) > 0 then
			local list = shapes :: { any }
			local first = list[1]
			local material = if typeof(first) == "table" then first.material else nil
			local named = typeof(material) == "string" and material ~= ""
			if #list == 1 then
				return if named
					then string.format("Fill terrain with %s", material)
					else "Fill terrain"
			end
			return if named
				then string.format("Fill %s, starting with %s", plural(#list, "terrain shape"), material)
				else string.format("Fill %s", plural(#list, "terrain shape"))
		end
		return "Fill terrain"
	end,

	end,

	end,

		local count = if typeof(params.slots) == "table" then #params.slots else 0
		if action == "set" then
			return string.format("Set %s", plural(count, "terrain material"))
		elseif action == "reset" then

		end
		return "List terrain materials"
	end,

	end,

--[[
	What kind of work an op is, for anything that wants to colour it.

	Grouped by what it does to the place rather than by which handler owns it,
	because that is the distinction someone watching cares about: reading is
	safe and constant, writing changes their game, and running executes code.
]]
local KINDS: { [string]: string } = {
	discover = "read",
	client = "read",
	studio = "read",
	viewport = "read",
	capture = "read",
	instances = "write",
	geometry = "write",
	assets = "write",
	world = "write",
	exec = "run",
	playtest = "run",
	character = "run",
	-- Live keys and clicks into a running playtest are an action, not a read,
	-- and belong beside character/exec rather than defaulting to "read".
	input = "run",
	debug = "debug",
	perf = "debug",
	api = "read",
	-- Only feeds Script Analysis; no instance or source changes.
	analysis = "read",
	device = "read",
	-- Casts and overlap tests only look; nothing in the group writes.
	spatial = "read",
	-- Wiring and graph building write; `audio.inspect` is carved out below.
	audio = "write",
	--[[
		Absent groups defaulted to "read", which is the wrong way round for a
		default: a missing entry made `terrain.clear` and `data.set` -- one of
		which erases the map and the other of which overwrites a player's save
		with no undo -- show in the panel with the same weight as an inspect.
		A kind is a warning, so the ones that change things are named here
		explicitly.
	]]
	terrain = "write",
	generate = "write",
	data = "write",
	-- Applies files to the place; the reads inside the group are carved out below.
	sync = "write",
}

function Phrase.kindOf(op: string, params: { [string]: any }?): string
	local group = string.match(op, "^([^%.]+)%.") or op
	-- Reads within the script group, writes outside it: a script edit changes
	-- the game, a read or a grep does not, and they are far apart in weight.
	if group == "script" then
		local action = string.match(op, "%.(.+)$") or ""
		return if action == "read" or action == "grep" then "read" else "write"
	end
	-- Same shape as the script group: one read sitting among writes.
	if op == "audio.inspect" then
		return "read"
	end
	if op == "terrain.stats" then
		return "read"
	end
	if op == "terrain.materials" and (params == nil or params.action == nil or params.action == "list") then
		return "read"
	end
	if op == "sync.scan" or op == "sync.shape" or op == "sync.revisions" or op == "sync.read" or op == "sync.changes" or op == "sync.classes" or op == "sync.export" then
		return "read"
	end
	return KINDS[group] or "read"
end

--[[
	The readable form of one command.

	Never throws and never yields: this runs on the path that logs every call,
	including the ones that are about to fail, and a console that errors while
	describing an error would take the diagnosis with it.
]]
function Phrase.of(op: string, params: { [string]: any }?): string
	local describer = DESCRIBERS[op]
	if describer ~= nil then
		local ok, described = pcall(describer, params or {})
		if ok and typeof(described) == "string" and described ~= "" then
			return described
		end
	end

	-- Unknown op, or a describer that met a shape it did not expect. Tidy the
	-- wire name rather than inventing a subject for it: "instances.create"
	-- becomes "Instances create", which is honest about knowing no better.
	local group, action = string.match(op, "^([^%.]+)%.(.+)$")
	if group ~= nil and action ~= nil then
		return titleCase(group) .. " " .. action
	end
	return titleCase(op)
end

return Phrase

local New = Fusion.New
local Hydrate = Fusion.Hydrate

type Props = {
	[any]: any,
}

return function(props: Props): ImageLabel
	return Hydrate(New("ImageLabel") {
		BorderSizePixel = 0,
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
	})(props)
end
